articles.title: 'Really like his chess, not his personality': Russia No. 1 Nepo on Hans Niemann's 'FIDE must punish' remarks | Exclusive
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: Ian Nepomniachtchi, also known as \"Nepo\", has little doubt about Hans Niemann’s ability on the chessboard. Away from it, however, the Russi.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Ian Nepomniachtchi, also known as "Nepo", has little doubt about Hans Niemann’s ability on the chessboard. Away from it, however, the Russian grandmaster remains less impressed.Reacting to Niemann’s recent call for FIDE to punish players who make public accusations or insinuations, particularly involving young players, Nepomniachtchi said the American grandmaster “can’t stop playing the victim card”.“First of all, Hans can’t stop playing the victim card. He pretty much lives in that skin. I think there was a fair reason, from his online performances through many years, as far as I know, to be cautious about Hans himself,” Nepo, Russia’s No. 1 player, told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interaction on the sidelines of the Global Chess League (GCL).Despite the friction, Nepomniachtchi feels that Niemann has established himself as a strong player. “As for Hans right now, he proves himself as a very good and formidable player. I really like the way he plays chess, though I don’t like his personality. As a chess player, he plays quite well, and in certain openings, he’s quite good at,” he added.At the same time, Nepo also believes Niemann is quick to seize opportunities to provoke a reaction. “Whenever he has an opportunity to bite anyone and seek for some reaction, he immediately does this. Maybe for him, it’s fine for his overall image,” he said.Drawing a comparison with mixed martial arts star Conor McGregor, he said Niemann appears to have embraced a similarly controversial image in chess.“Conor McGregor has 'The Notorious' nickname in MMA. Hans surely tries to be some notorious chess player. So that’s what he does,” Nepomniachtchi said.What triggered the reaction from HansThe comments come after Niemann criticised Nepomniachtchi over remarks made during an online game against 14-year-old Canadian chess player Aaron Mendes.Mendes defeated Nepomniachtchi in Round 10 of the Titled Tuesday event on September 1. During his stream, Nepomniachtchi questioned Mendes’ decision to play an en passant capture instead of giving check.“I would have zero suspicions about this game, but his en passant instead of a check, it leaves a bad taste. Why? How? For what? Aaron, my friend… Fortunately, we will not play against Aaron again in the tournament, because we already learned our lesson from him,” Nepomniachtchi had said.Niemann subsequently called on FIDE to take action against players who make public accusations or insinuations, particularly when young players are involved.“FIDE must punish players for public accusations and insinuations, especially regarding a 14-year-old,” Niemann wrote on X, adding that genuine concerns should instead be taken to FIDE’s Ethics Commission.Nepo on Hans Niemann's "Untold: Chess Mates" documentary Asked about the Netflix documentary "Untold: Chess Mates", which revisits the cheating controversy surrounding Niemann, Nepomniachtchi said it did not reveal much that was new to him.“I was sort of inside of this. I was playing the same tournament. I didn’t find out anything new. Some of it was more or less obvious,” he revealed.“Everything was on the surface. But the most disappointing thing in the documentary is that there is no answer. I expected it as a usual chess fan.”Read Also: 8 months, Moscow-to-Munich flights, but now he is 'fed up': Behind Russia No. 1 Ian Nepomniachtchi's tattoosFor those looking to get introduced to chess, however, Nepomniachtchi had another recommendation. “If you want to get introduced to chess, I would better suggest you watch "The Queen of Chess" about Judit Polgar. That was an awesome one.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fans Outraged Over Lainey Wilson's 'College GameDay' Performance
articles.summary: They didn't love it.
articles.body:
ESPN kicked off its 40th season of "College GameDay" in Baton Rouge this Saturday. While the atmosphere at the start of the show was outstanding, the opening act was questionable to say the least.

It was announced earlier this week that country singer Lainey Wilson would be the first guest picker of the season for "College GameDay." The "Heart Like a Truck" singer said she'd perform a few songs during her time in Louisiana. What we didn't know though is that she'd open the show by singing "Comin' to Your City."

While this must have been an awesome opportunity for Wilson, the early responses to her performance haven't been positive. In fact, most fans said she sounded terrible on "College GameDay."

"This Lainey Wilson performance is cringe," one fan said. "Just give me a Saban rant on LSU."

"Get Lainey Wilson off my screen give me the old theme song version," a second fan wrote.

"I'd rather listen to chalk on a whiteboard than to listen to Lainey Wilson," another fan commented.

"Wow, this Lainey Wilson opening act is absolutely awful. You've messed up this tradition. And I'm a huge Lainey fan," another person replied.

This Saturday's episode of "College GameDay" will mark its 500th road show. That's an incredible achievement for the show that Lee Corso helped make famous.

There'll be plenty of laughs and entertaining segments on "College GameDay" before Kirk Herbstreit, Desmond Howard, Nick Saban and Pat McAfee make their predictions for tonight's showdown between Clemson and LSU.

We can't wait to see how McAfee fires up the LSU crowd this Saturday.

articles.title: Auburn football report card: Grading the Tigers after Baylor win
articles.summary: Here's our report card for Auburn football after a thrilling finish to a win against Baylor.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — It was difficult to expect much of what transpired between Auburn football and Baylor — certainly that it came down to the wire and that a goal-line stand gave the Tigers a 17-16 victory.

There were some surprises — good and bad alike — for Auburn , and it'll have plenty to improve upon as it continues its first season under Alex Golesh .

Here's our postgame report card of the Tigers' performance:

There were flashes, and what Brown did to give Auburn its go-ahead score displayed his value. But he still tossed three interceptions, and his offensive line surrendered double-digit tackles for loss. That'll need plenty of work.

It felt like a vintage Auburn performance on the defense end. Baylor made it look human on more than one occasion, but the Tigers buckled down in terms of scoring opportunities, giving up points on just two of its opponent's 13 drives.

Hudson Kaak had an effective day with half of his punts pinned inside the 20-yard line, and Alex McPherson ultimately split a pair of field goal attempts. A serviceable day from Auburn's specialists.

Golesh acknowledged more than once this week that Week 1 can be unpredictable sometimes. It felt unpredictable come game time, and while there may have only been so much to scout, Auburn looked unprepared for certain aspects of the Bears.

The sophomore safety's goal-line stop saved the day. Plus, he had double-digit tackles, two tackles for loss and a forced fumble.

Auburn's defense does most of the heavy lifting for its team grade. Clearly, the Tigers passed. There's still so much ample room for improvement.

articles.title: Weather Cancels Darlington Qualifying Tyler Reddick Lands Pole
articles.summary: The NASCAR Cup Series playoff opener at Darlington Raceway got an unexpected twist Saturday afternoon. Practice and qualifying for the Cook Out Southern 500...
articles.body:
The NASCAR Cup Series playoff opener at Darlington Raceway got an unexpected twist Saturday afternoon.

Practice and qualifying for the Cook Out Southern 500 were canceled because of lightning and severe weather in the area , meaning drivers never got the opportunity to put down a qualifying lap. NASCAR ultimately used its established metric to determine Sunday's starting lineup.

The weather delay began before drivers could get meaningful track time.

Lightning repeatedly moved into the area around Darlington, forcing NASCAR to delay the on-track session. Even though significant rain never arrived, the continued lightning made it impossible for officials to safely continue. After multiple delays, NASCAR eventually canceled both practice and qualifying.

That means teams will head into the opening race of the 2026 Chase without the normal practice and qualifying data they would have expected.

The cancellation turned out to be great news for Tyler Reddick .

Reddick will start Sunday's Southern 500 from the pole position in his No. 45 23XI Racing Toyota. Daniel Suárez will join him on the front row. Ryan Preece, Denny Hamlin and Michael McDowell round out the top five.

For Reddick, it's an especially important starting spot. He enters the playoffs as one of the championship contenders and already has a Darlington victory this season.

Reddick called the situation a "best-case scenario" for his team after the cancellation, noting that his confidence was already high heading into the weekend.

While Reddick benefited, several playoff contenders weren't nearly as fortunate.

Kyle Larson will start 25th, Ryan Blaney 24th, Ross Chastain 23rd and William Byron 20th. Carson Hocevar will start 34th, while Chris Buescher starts 35th.

That could make Sunday's race even more chaotic.

Darlington is already one of NASCAR's most difficult tracks, and starting position can be especially important when drivers are trying to protect championship points.

The Southern 500 is the first race of the 10-race NASCAR playoff , making the cancellation even more significant.

With no practice and no qualifying laps, teams will have to rely heavily on their previous experience and simulator work. Drivers starting deeper in the field will have to fight through traffic at one of the toughest tracks on the schedule.

The weather may have canceled qualifying, but it didn't cancel the drama. The 2026 Chase is officially underway, and Darlington is already throwing a curveball at the championship contenders.

articles.title: Zheng, Potapova pull off upsets to reach US Open last 16
articles.summary: Zheng Qinwen won the last seven games to stun Madison Keys and reach the US Open last 16 in a day of upsets that dented American hopes on Saturday at Flushin...
articles.body:
Zheng Qinwen won the last seven games to stun Madison Keys and reach the US Open last 16 in a day of upsets that dented American hopes on Saturday at Flushing Meadows.

Fourth-seeded Coco Gauff battled through in straight sets, but Americans were hard hit with ninth-seeded Taylor Fritz and 2025 finalist Amanda Anisimova following Keys out the door.

Fifth-seeded French Open finalist Flavio Cobolli of Italy also fell to 21-year-old Alexander Blockx.

Zheng saved a match point in her 1-6, 7-6 (7/3), 7-5 triumph over Keys, the 2025 Australian Open champion and a US Open finalist back in 2017.

After coming through the second-set tiebreaker, Zheng appeared to be out of steam in the final set.

The former world number four had to come through qualifying after a lengthy recovery from elbow surgery saw her ranking plummet.

Keys raced to a 5-0 lead in the third but Zheng had a last stand in her. She saved match point at 5-1 and just kept rolling, Keys's increasing frustration showing as she banged her head with her racquet after one lost point.

"I just told myself keep holding every single point, never give up, stay there. And somehow little by little it just happened," Zheng said.

Zheng, currently ranked 121st in the world, will face six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek for a place in the quarter-finals.

Swiatek saved three set points in the second set, dominating both tiebreakers in her tight 7-6 (7/3), 7-6 (7/3) win over Czech Maria Bouzkova.

Belgium's Blockx shocked Cobolli 6-7 (4/7), 6-3, 6-0, 6-3, winning 11 straight games from 3-2 down in the second set as he reached the second week of a Grand Slam for the first time.

"I think this was one of my craziest experiences so far in my career," Blockx said after firing 17 aces past Cobolli.

"After the first set I told myself to stay calm. I wasn't playing bad. I know deep inside I'm a fighter and I will fight until the last ball and it paid off today."

Blockx next faces Francisco Cerundolo, who rallied from two sets down to upset ninth-seeded Fritz 3-6, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4.

Down 4-3 on serve in the final set, the 24th seed from Argentina fought back from 0-40 down to hold, coming up with a trio of booming serves and a thundering forehand before taking the game with another service winner.

Austrian Anastasia Potapova further dented US hopes with her 6-2, 7-5 victory over Anisimova.

Potapova reached the US Open fourth round for the first time, and will face fifth-seeded French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, who beat Nikola Bartunkova 6-2, 7-6 (7/5).

Former champion Gauff shook off a slow start to beat Spain's Cristina Bucsa 6-3, 6-4, relying on her defensive skills as she climbed out of a 3-1 hole in the opening set.

"She's a tricky player, so it's tough to get rhythm," Gauff said. "Happy with how I fought through even when I wasn't playing my best."

Gauff said she'd seen the US trio go down before her match, but it didn't affect how she approached her match.

"Upsets are a thing, but at the end of the day, anybody can lose," she said. "I go into it with that mindset, and I think, if anything, it makes me have my guard up all the time, which makes me play better."

Men's top seed Alexander Zverev was again due to close out the night session, taking on Chile's Alejandro Tabilo.

In two five-set matches, both spilling into the early hours of the morning, the German has already spent nine hours and 26 minutes on court.

Zverev says he feels fine physically, but he knows he will have to play better if he wants to add a second Grand Slam title to the French Open trophy he captured this year.

articles.title: No. 22 Iowa uses defense, Moulton's running game to beat Northern Illinois 40-0
articles.summary: Kamari Moulton ran for a career-high 183 yards and two touchdowns and No. 22 Iowa’s defense shut down Northern Illinois in a 40-0 victory Saturday in the sea...
articles.body:
IOWA CITY, Iowa (AP) — Kamari Moulton ran for a career-high 183 yards and two touchdowns and No. 22 Iowa's defense shut down Northern Illinois in a 40-0 victory Saturday in the season opener for both teams.

Moulton, Iowa's leading rusher last season, passed his previous career high of 114 yards in the first quarter, when he had 132 yards with touchdown runs of 50 and 37 yards.

It was the first regular-season look at the Iowa quarterback battle between Hank Brown and Jeremy Hecklinski, who came into the game sharing the top spot on the depth chart.

Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz said earlier in the week that each would get playing time in the game. Brown got the start, leading the Hawkeyes to touchdowns on their first three series before Hecklinski made his first appearance.

Brown finished 12 of 20 passing for 129 yards. Hecklinski was 7 of 16 for 76 yards with an interception. Brown threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Tony Diaz on Iowa's opening series of the game, and Hecklinski threw a 8-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Williams in the second quarter.

Caden Buhr added two field goals for the Hawkeyes, and Evan James had a 77-yard punt return for a touchdown in the second half.

The Hawkeyes held a 507-120 edge in offensive yards. Northern Illinois, which had 14 yards in the first half, did not get its first first down until the third quarter, and that came on a pass-interference penalty against Iowa.

There was no clear leader in Iowa's quarterback competition. The offense moved efficiently under Brown in the first quarter, but Hecklinski had his good moments as well. It's a question that likely will hang over the Hawkeyes over the next couple of weeks.

Northern Illinois: Hosts Illinois State next Saturday.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham’s hilarious business idea with Diana Taurasi has fans imagining a WNBA yacht party
articles.summary: International Sports News: Sophie Cunningham has found plenty of ways to keep WNBA fans talking, both on and off the court. The Indiana Fever guard recently shared an unexpected.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham has found plenty of ways to keep WNBA fans talking, both on and off the court. The Indiana Fever guard recently shared an unexpectedly ambitious idea for her dream business, and it has little to do with basketball. Her plan involves a yacht, endless sunshine, drinks and one of the biggest names in WNBA history, Diana Taurasi.Sophie Cunningham’s dream business has a Diana Taurasi twistCunningham was asked what kind of business she would create if she could team up with another WNBA player. Instead of naming a teammate or choosing something connected to basketball, she went in a much more relaxed direction.Her pick was Taurasi, the legendary former WNBA star who built one of the most decorated careers in women's basketball. Cunningham's reason for choosing her potential business partner was refreshingly direct."If you were going to start a business with another WNBA player, who would it be?""I like that," she says in response to the question.After taking a moment to consider the idea, Cunningham revealed that she would choose Taurasi and build the business around a yacht."Because she has the finances," Cunningham explains.The concept sounds less like a traditional startup and more like a floating vacation for basketball fans. Cunningham imagined spending time on a boat, either on a lake or out at sea, with good weather, drinks and plenty of opportunities to relax."And then, the business would be being on a yacht, on a boat, on a lake or on the ocean, drinks flowing, you're getting a nice tan. But, definitely, budget, not mine."The comment captures Cunningham's playful personality. Rather than pitching a serious investment plan, she leaned into the fun of imagining what life could look like if money and logistics were not a concern.The interviewer then compared the concept to the reality series "Below Deck," which follows crews working aboard luxury yachts."You guys can start your own 'Below Deck?'""I like that," she says, laughing. "Absolutely."Sophie Cunningham’s growing profile beyond basketballWhile a WNBA yacht venture with Taurasi remains a fantasy for now, Cunningham's growing popularity has opened plenty of doors away from basketball.The Fever guard recently passed 4 million followers on Instagram, giving her an enormous platform beyond the court. That kind of reach can make athletes attractive partners for consumer brands, particularly when their personalities connect with fans.Cunningham has already stepped into that space through a partnership with Once Upon a Coconut, a coconut water brand. The collaboration fits naturally with her athletic career and public image, especially as hydration remains an important part of an athlete's daily routine.Her business interests may be developing, but the yacht idea stands out for a different reason. It shows the lighter side of Cunningham and her ability to turn a simple interview question into an entertaining vision.Whether it ever becomes reality is another matter. For now, the idea of Cunningham and Taurasi hosting fans on a luxury yacht is a fun glimpse at what might happen when two WNBA personalities decide to take their talents offshore.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A pioneer until the end: Katie Taylor’s historic boxing journey ends with emotional Croke Park farewell
articles.summary: From St. Fergal's Boxing Club in Bray to Croke Park, Katie Taylor set the standard.
articles.body:
Once upon a time, one DM changed everything, not just for women's boxing but for the sport as a whole. After fighting to break into the sport, Katie Taylor's exchange with Matchroom Boxing's Eddie Hearn led to a remarkable journey that ended in the hallowed halls of Croke Park.

September 5, 2026: A finale fitting for a true trailblazer.

Taylor's career came to a close on Saturday, in front of over 80,000 passionate fans who came from near and far to watch "The Bray Bomber" in action.

Taylor beat Flora Pili by unanimous decision via a classic Taylor performance. She became a three-time undisputed champion, twice holding all the gold at super lightweight. An emotional Taylor had the ring all to herself after as she put her gloves and titles in the middle of it.

From her entrance to the announcement of her win, it was one of the most moving sendoffs in boxing history.

Her fans would have traveled anywhere to see her. Taylor has showcased her skills in legendary arenas, from the The O2 London, Madison Square Garden, AT&T Stadium, and the 3Arena. Those were always on the table for her last fight. But there was one venue Hearn and Taylor insisted on for her last dance. It's a place they've attempted to book for years.

"It's Croke Park or nothing for me," Taylor said.

Croke Park, the home of the Gaelic Athletic Association, has seen its fair share of triumphs and tragedies. Mayo ended a 75-year drought to win the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship. There was also Bloody Sunday during the Irish War of Independence. Legends have stood on that pitch, from Michael Hogan to Muhammad Ali. Taylor now joins them.

Her 30-year-journey to get here is something special. Taylor boxed as a boy, hiding her hair in a cap because girls weren't allowed to compete. At 15, Taylor fought in Ireland's first sanctioned women's boxing match. She competed in the Olympics in a time when women's boxing at the Olympic Games was initially deemed impossible. Songs were made in her honor as she won gold.

Holding various amateur titles, Taylor wanted more. She reached out to Hearn via a DM. Hearn took a gamble and made her one of the faces of Matchroom Boxing.

"I've been seriously considering turning pro over the last few months. I think I could do, for women's pro boxing, what I did for the amateur game: bring it into focus and generate a serious interest. I already have a global profile and a great fan base. Of course, the pro game is impossible without a great promoter," Taylor said .

Taylor climbed up the ladder, beating some of the best in the sport. She made an impact in the U.S., competing in Boston, Philadelphia, and New York. In the latter state, Taylor engaged in an epic Fight of the Year contender against Delfine Persoon, stealing the show even with a main event featuring Anthony Joshua. She became undisputed in the division and had another classic with Persoon and later Natasha Jonas.

Taylor became undisputed at super lightweight and avenged the only loss of her career against Chantelle Cameron. Between then, she competed against Amanda Serrano in three historic fights. The first fight was the first women's contest to headline Madison Square Garden. It earned her the 2022 Fight of the Year . The rematch was watched by millions , with Taylor once again stealing the show, this time with the main event being Jake Paul vs. Mike Tyson. The third was the first all-women's card inside MSG .

Hearn has been Team Taylor since day one and has attempted to sway even the biggest doubters. The efforts have worked, even in a sport that has as many critics as it does admirers.

"Boxing is a really toxic world," Hearn told The BBC . "There's always people who don't like people but there isn't one female fighter you could find that wouldn't go, 'she's incredible'. "She's just so loved, there's no airs or graces. She's not there for the fame, she's not there for the money, it's purely her faith, the love of the sport and trying to set an example."

Former dance partners, promoters, and young fans showed up to fight week, honoring all that Taylor has done. The hope is that more women, from Ireland and beyond, will follow in her footsteps.

"She's fighting on the doorstep of our club now on the biggest stage, in front of 80,000 people. It's a brilliant legacy for the girls to follow," Frankie Molloy, 9, of Corinthians Boxing Club, told The Irish Times .

Taylor, now a three-time undisputed champion, rides off into the sunset knowing she's done all she could for women's boxing and Ireland itself. Fans who followed her journey appreciated her efforts, with cheers and tears of joy showcased all across Croke Park.

From St. Fergal's Boxing Club in Bray all the way to Croke Park, Taylor set the standard. She carried a nation on her back. Taylor ends her career on her terms, fulfilling a dream.

Simply put, she did it the Katie Taylor way.

articles.title: Zheng goes from 5-0 and match point down to victory
articles.summary: Zheng Qinwen fights back from 5-0 down in the deciding set and stares down match point to stun American 22nd seed Madison Keys.
articles.body:
Zheng Qinwen described her US Open third-round comeback win over Madison Keys as a "very dramatic match" - but that is somewhat of an understatement.

The Olympic champion, who had to come through qualifying to reach the main draw, found herself 5-0 and match point down in the third set against Keys.

But Zheng held firm and reeled off seven games in a row to secure a remarkable 1-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 victory over the 22nd seed and crowd favourite.

Keys, who won the 2025 Australian Open, appeared to be cruising towards a commanding victory after wrapping up the opening set in just 23 minutes.

But Zheng, who is rebuilding her career after undergoing elbow surgery last year, rallied, clinching it on a tie-break before snatching victory from the jaws of defeat against the American.

Zheng threw herself to the floor in relief and reflected afterwards on a difficult 12 months in which she has questioned if she will rediscover her form.

"Finally, a bit of luck is on my side," the 23-year-old said.

"I am just telling myself ever give up. Somehow, little by little, it's just happened.

"Tennis sometimes feels like rollercoaster. You see many times people have a match point, but at the end we made a comeback."

The Chinese star is the first qualifier to reach the women's fourth round at the US Open since Britain's Emma Raducanu, who went on to win the 2021 title.

'I forgot how to compete' - but Zheng rises again

Three months ago, Zheng could not hold back her tears in a news conference after a first-round exit at the French Open.

It was her first Grand Slam since undergoing surgery in July 2025 to correct a chronic injury caused by small pieces of bone floating in the elbow.

The injury came after a breakthrough 2024 where she reached the Australian Open final, won Olympic gold and made the US Open quarter-finals.

She had also enjoyed a promising start to 2025 before injury struck, advancing to the last eight at Roland Garros and climbing to a career-high of fourth in the world rankings.

It was understandable, therefore, why Zheng found a first-round defeat in Paris this year difficult to take - even if it was to eventual runner-up Maja Chwalinska after nine months on the sidelines.

Her ranking dropped as low as 160 and she had to contest a Grand Slam qualifying event for the first time in four years.

"After coming back from injury I felt I lost the energy and I forgot how to compete," she said.

Zheng seems to have recaptured some of her best form, having been taken to three sets in four of her six matches in New York so far.

She did not meet criteria for a protected ranking - for which players can apply if they are out injured for at least six months - because she made an early comeback to play her home tournament in Beijing in October 2025.

That meant she had to come through qualifying - something she found difficult to accept.

"I was even crying after I won the third match to reach the main draw," Zheng said.

"The main draw is just the beginning where all the players start. That was my beginning before.

"I fight so hard just to start like everyone else. For me, that was really not easy."

Her composure was on display against Keys - especially at 5-4 0-15 down, when she was forced to stop her service motion after a baby started crying in the crowd.

"If it's adult, probably I will look at him very hard or start to speak, but it's just a baby," Zheng joked.

"I can't do anything, you know? It's just a baby."

Zheng went on to win the next four points to level the tie - and the rest was history.

articles.title: Texas makes emphatic opening statement in routing Texas State with No. 1 Ohio State up next
articles.summary: Arch Manning threw four touchdown passes in three-plus quarters as Texas' offense was highly efficient in rolling up a big lead on regional foe Texas State t...
articles.body:
AUSTIN - Texas delivered exactly was expected.

Senior quarterback Arch Manning threw four touchdown passes, two of them to celebrated transfer wide receiver Cam Coleman , and the fifth-ranked Longhorns raced to a dominant 59-7 win over Texas State on a steamy Saturday at Royal-Memorial Stadium.

Manning started what may be his final collegiate season with a highly efficient game. He completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four scores before leaving midway through the third quarter, connecting with Coleman twice and Ryan Wingo and Hollywood Smothers once each.

The Longhorns were very effective, scoring touchdowns on six of their first seven possessions and burying their neighbors down I-35. Backup KJ Lacey Jr. relieved Manning during the third quarter and led Texas to a score on his first series.

Expectations have rarely been higher for Texas , coming off a 10-3 season and a bowl win over Michigan but missing a spot in the College Football Playoff.

The Longhorns square off at home next Saturday night against preseason No. 1 Ohio State , which clobbered 50-point underdog Ball State 56-3 on Saturday.

Texas' defense under new coordinator Will Muschamp produced three takeaways, including an interception by transfer linebacker Rasheem Biles , and held one of college football's most explosive offenses to a single touchdown and 321 total yards.

Texas State, which is projected to finish anywhere from fourth to sixth in the reconfigured Pac-12, has won three straight bowl games but was no match for one of the nation's best teams. The Bobcats' new kicker, Dylan Cunanan from Toledo, was wide left on two field goal tries from 24 and 35 yards.

Texas jumped to a 28-0 lead in the first half, scoring on its first three offensive possessions and on Graceson Littleton 's 59-yard fumble return. The lead could have grown, but the Longhorns had to settle for a 28-7 advantage at halftime when Manning was looking for Emmett Mosley V and threw into double coverage for an easy interception by rover Ryan Nolan .

The defense was active and punishing against an effective Bobcats offense that ranked fifth in the nation last year and has averaged 36.5 points a game in head coach G.J. Kinne's three seasons in San Marcos.

Three different Longhorns scored on offense in the first two quarters, but Texas State had just 58 fewer yards at the half than its host.

Manning completed 15 of 20 throws for 203 yards and threw a pair of touchdown passes on Texas' first two possessions.

He completed an easy 6-yard pass to Coleman and an 8-yard flip pass to Wingo on the jet sweep. Transfer running back Raleek Brown scored on a 13-yard burst up the middle.

Texas needed just six plays to get on the scoreboard. Hollywood Smothers juked cornerback Amarion Atwood out of his cleats on a 45-yard gain on the Longhorns' first offensive snap of the game, and Manning found a wide open Coleman for an easy 6-yard touchdown in the left flat when Atwood fell down.

This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald drops update on Terrion Arnold amid commissioner’s exempt list stint
articles.summary: Mike Macdonald has made it clear that Terrion Arnold is staying prepared despite being unable to practice or play for the Seattle Seahawks at present. The co...
articles.body:
Mike Macdonald has made it clear that Terrion Arnold is staying prepared despite being unable to practice or play for the Seattle Seahawks at present.

The cornerback remains on the NFL's commissioner's exempt list, but his current situation has not stopped him from working with the Seahawks in other ways.

Arnold is allowed to be at the team's facility and attend meetings, providing him with an opportunity to become familiar with Seattle's defensive system while he waits for clarity on his status.

Terrion Arnold continues to prepare with Seahawks

Macdonald offered an update on what Arnold has been doing during this period, highlighting the cornerback's focus on understanding the Seahawks' defence.

"He's learning the heck out of our defense," Macdonald said, according to video shared by Hawk Blogger's Brian Nemhauser on his X.

The Seahawks head coach also explained that Arnold's preparation is not limited to learning the system. Macdonald said the cornerback would "keep training and stay ready for if and when there's an opportunity."

Arnold therefore remains engaged with the team despite the restrictions surrounding his current status.

His inability to practice or play means there is still no clarity on when he can take the next step on the field. In the meantime, Seattle can continue the installation process with Arnold through meetings and his work at the team facility.

If an opportunity to return eventually arrives, the preparation Arnold is doing now could help him make the football adjustment after his time away from practice and games.

articles.title: 5 Oklahoma State football takeaways from ugly loss to Tulsa in debut of Eric Morris era
articles.summary: The Oklahoma State Cowboys saw their 11-game season-opening win streak end with a 24-10 loss to Tulsa in Eric Morris' debut as OSU football coach.
articles.body:
TULSA — Oklahoma State carried an 11-game season-opening win streak, the fourth-longest in FBS. It didn't carry it out of H.A. Chapman Stadium.

Tulsa defeated OSU 24-10 on Saturday, opening the Eric Morris era in Stillwater on a sour note. The Golden Hurricane have now beaten OSU twice in a row for the first time since 1950-52, when it happened three consecutive times.

Oklahoma State Cowboys vs Tulsa Golden Hurricane in Week 1 college football, see photos

OSU felt left tackle Jacob Sexton 's absence

After missing 12 games last year at OU with a season-ending injury, new Cowboy left tackle Jacob Sexton got to play only six snaps in his 2026 return.

Sexton fell to the ground after getting undercut by a blocked Tulsa defender. Sexton sprawled on the turf for five minutes getting medical attention. Sexton was carted off with an air cast on his right leg .

Later in that drive on fourth-and-1 from the Tulsa 3-yard line, OSU running back Caleb Hawkins tried the left side of the line of scrimmage and was stuffed.

On a third-and-12 on OSU's second drive of the game, Tulsa sent a blitz from the left side. The Cowboys were unable to slide protection and quarterback Drew Mestemaker was hit for a loss of 8, ending the drive.

Tulsa, not Oklahoma State, generated the explosive plays

Big offensive plays were expected in the game. The surprising part is they came from only Tulsa.

Tulsa's offense broke big plays for 56 yards and 47 yards in the first half. OSU's longest play of the game was a 27-yard pass to receiver Wyatt Young in the fourth quarter.

In the first quarter, Tulsa receiver Oran Singleton beat junior cornerback Kollin Lewis down the right sideline and caught an over-the-shoulder pass for a 56-yard gain.

In the second quarter, Tulsa quarterback Baylor Hayes hung in the pocket and threw a rainbow pass into one-on-one coverage to Tulsa receiver Jimmy Calloway. Calloway wrestled the jump ball away from LaDainian Fields at the OSU 1-yard line for a gain of 47 yards. The play led to a touchdown.

In the first half, Caleb Hawkins split work

Hawkins, a 6-foot, 219 pound running machine, was OSU's most effective rusher in the first half. Morris prioritized keeping him fresh.

Hawkins nearly split work in the first half with Tarleton State transfer Tre Page III . Even in some short-yardage situations OSU turned to Page, listed at 5-foot-8, 184 pounds.

In the first half, Hawkins rushed 10 times for 54 yards (5.4 average) and Page III ran seven times for 19 yards.

Inside the Tulsa 10-yard line on OSU's first drive of the game Morris twice called runs for Page III, who rushed for 7 yards and then was stuffed for no gain. OSU couldn't cash the touchdown in.

OSU's third drive of the game ended when Page fumbled on a fourth-and-1 from its own 32. In the third quarter, senior Ayo Adeyi received his first carry of the game on fourth-and-1 and didn't convert.

Morris turned the keys to Hawkins in the second half and Hawkins finished with 18 carries for 79 yards. Page III didn't carry the ball in the second half.

Two fumbles could have made this thing worse

Even after Tulsa took a 17-3 lead midway through the third quarter, the game never felt out of reach. That was fortunate for the Cowboys.

Fumbles from Page III and Mestemaker twice handed the ball to the Golden Hurricane on the wrong side of the 50-yard line. Both times, the Cowboy defense bowed up and forced Tulsa kicker Marlon Hauck on the field.

Hauck missed a 31-yard attempt in the second quarter and a 40-yard attempt in the third, sending both footballs wide right sailing into the Case Athletic Complex that overlooks the field.

Last season under Morris, North Texas converted 62.2% of its fourth-down conversions.

This year, Morris' OSU offense is off to a 33.3% start.

It started out well, with Hawkins picking up a fourth-and-1 with a 3-yard plow up the middle on the game's first drive.

First quarter: Fourth-and-1 (Page III fumble)

Third quarter: Fourth-and-1 (Adeyi stuffed for no gain)

Fourth quarter: Fourth-and-1 ( Miles Coleman reception for zero yards)

Mestemaker got the fourth-down woes on track late in the third quarter in a do-or-die fourth-and-7 where he found receiver Justin Bowick for a touchdown.

articles.title: Extreme heat stops Washburn-Colorado Mines before overtime, leaving game a 16-16 tie
articles.summary: Washburn and Colorado School of Mines played to a rare 16-16 tie Saturday when extreme heat in central Kansas forced officials from the Division II schools a...
articles.body:
TOPEKA, Kan. (AP) — Washburn and Colorado School of Mines played to a rare 16-16 tie Saturday when extreme heat in central Kansas forced officials from the Division II schools and the Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association to halt the game before starting overtime.

The kickoff already had been moved to 9 a.m. to avoid the worst of the record-setting heat. But the temperature was approaching triple digits and the heat index well over 100 degrees Fahrenheit (38 Celsius) when the fourth quarter ended in a deadlock. The two teams along with league officials and the referees engaged in a lengthy discussion before calling the game a tie.

"Obviously the weather is hot. There's no way around it," Washburn coach Zach Watkins said, "and there are decisions made way above the coaches. But it's all about keeping the kids safe. It's the weather, the timing, the coming back from it.

"I just got done talking with the team," Watkins said, "and we're 1-0-1 and we move on."

The last tie in major college football happened in 1995, when Wisconsin and Illinois finished 3-3. Overtime was introduced before the following season, effectively ending the chance for tie games across all divisions.

Logan Madden had 268 yards passing and two touchdowns for the host Ichabods, who had opened the season with a win over Truman State. Joseph Capra had 214 yards passing and a touchdown for the Orediggers, who lost to Western Oregon last week.

articles.title: Qinwen Zheng stuns No. 22 Madison Keys with late rally at US Open
articles.summary: Trailing 5-0 in the third set against Madison Keys, Qinwen Zheng staged a thrilling comeback by winning the next seven games.
articles.body:
Trailing 5-0 in the third set against No. 22 seed Madison Keys, Qinwen Zheng staged a thrilling comeback by winning the next seven games to secure a 1-6, 7-6 (3), 7-5 victory on Saturday, Sept. 5 and reach the fourth round of the US Open in New York.

Zheng, the 2024 Olympic gold medalist from China, held serve while trailing 5-0, then saved a match point with Keys serving at 5-1. Zheng broke the 2017 U.S. Open runner-up three times during her seven-game run before serving out the improbable victory in two hours, 28 minutes.

"I'm just telling myself (to) keep holding every single point, never give up, stay there and somehow, little by little, it just happened," Zheng said in her on-court interview.

In 2024, when she won gold at the Olympics after advancing to the Australian Open final, Zheng was ranked as high as No. 4. However, following right elbow surgery, she is at No. 121 and had to make it through qualifying just to reach the main draw at the U.S. Open.

"After the surgery, it was not easy," Zheng said. "It felt like I lost a bit of my energy on the tennis court. I've been through really tough (moments) these last three, four, five months.

"But we've been working really hard … and yeah, the hard work finally paid off a bit. I want to say thanks to my team first for bringing me here. Let's keep going."

Keys, who won her previous match after facing five match points, came out firing in the first set, winning in 23 minutes after capturing 20 of the final 23 points. Zheng turned it around in the second set, which went to a tiebreaker, and won six of the last seven points with three winners to force the decisive third set.

Up next for Zheng will be Polish No. 8 seed Iga Swiatek, a former world No. 1 who defeated No. 25 seed Marie Bouzkova of the Czech Republic 7-6 (3), 7-6 (3) to reach the fourth round.

Zheng wasn't the only player to pull an upset, as No. 24 seed Anastasia Potapova of Austria took down No. 10 Amanda Anisimova 6-2, 7-5 in one hour, 39 minutes.

Potapova, who was on the verge of falling out of the top 100 this spring, has worked her way back into the top 25 as she advanced to the fourth round of the U.S. Open for the first time.

After breezing through the first set, Potapova was broken twice as Anisimova took the lead, but the Austrian broke back both times en route to the straight-sets victory.

"Well, to be honest, we had tactics before the match, which don't match my game, so it already was not easy," Potapova said in her press conference. "But the way I managed to use the tactics, I think it's one of the best games that I've ever had."

Anisimova, who advanced to the final at Wimbledon and the U.S. Open in 2025 and reached the Australian Open quarterfinals this year, was ousted in the third round of the last three Grand Slams this year. She converted just 3 of 16 break-point chances, compared to 6 of 8 for Potapova, a native of Russia who now represents Austria.

Potapova will next face Russian No. 5 seed Mirra Andreeva, who took out unseeded Czech Nikola Bartunkova 6-2, 7-6 (5).

Other winners Saturday included No. 4 seed Coco Gauff, who defeated unseeded Spaniard Cristina Bucsa 6-3, 6-4 to reach the Round of 16 for the fifth consecutive year, and No. 21 seed Anna Kalinskaya of Russia, who defeated Elina Svitolina of Ukraine 6-3, 2-6, 6-3.

For Gauff, it marks the fifth consecutive year she has reached the second week of the U.S. Open.

"I feel like I'm definitely used to getting the week 2s now, because I feel like I woke up today and I was like, 'oh, we're already in round 3,'" Gauff said in her on-court interview after the match. So I think that's a good sign, just feeling like I'm not feeling tired."

Gauff is also into the Round of 16 for the 11th time in the past 13 majors and has yet to drop a set at this year's U.S. Open.

"Just enjoying the experiences out here. Obviously, there's a lot of pressure here as an American in trying to do well. Everybody wants to win this tournament, but I think for Americans it's even more special."

Later Saturday, No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan faces unseeded Yuliia Starodubtseva of Ukraine, No. 13 seed Naomi Osaka of Japan takes on 23rd-seeded Elise Mertens of Belgium and No. 14 seed Iva Jovic opposes Alexandra Eala, the No. 17 seed from the Philippines.

articles.title: Newcomers Hollywood Smothers, Cam Coleman star as Texas begins year with Texas State rout
articles.summary: Cam Coleman scored twice and Hollywood Smothers shined in his Texas debut as the fifth-ranked Longhorns strolled to a season-opening win over Texas State on...
articles.body:
A season that the Texas football team hopes ends in January began with a win in September.

Cam Coleman and Raleek Brown scored twice and Hollywood Smothers also made a good first impression in Austin as No. 5 Texas strolled to a 59-7 triumph over Texas State on Saturday. In the 52-point victory at Royal-Memorial Stadium, the Longhorns forced three turnovers while Ryan Wingo contributed 121 receiving yards and Arch Manning passed for 305 yards and four touchdowns while completing 20 of his 27 attempts.

The fifth season-opening win in Steve Sarkisian's six-year tenure - and the third-biggest blowout of the Sarkisian era - preserves the stakes for next week's scintillating home showdown with No. 1 Ohio State .

Texas doesn't slow down after strong start

Texas (1-0) added 22 transfers this offseason, and a couple of those immediately introduced themselves to the fans who braved the 96-degree heat to get their first peek of the Longhorns in 248 days. Smothers ripped off a 45-yard run on UT's first snap. After the North Carolina State transfer inched the Longhorns five yards closer to the end zone on two runs, Coleman hauled in a 6-yard touchdown pass - the ex-Auburn standout's first score in burnt orange.

And with that four-play scoring drive, the Longhorns were off and running.

Thanks to an 8-yard touchdown catch by Wingo, Texas exited the first quarter leading 14-0. Texas kept scoring during the second quarter as Brown, a former Arizona State Sun Devil, ran for a 13-yard touchdown and Graceson Littleton returned a fumble for a 59-yard score. An end-zone interception thrown in the final seconds by Manning prevented Texas from scoring on all four of its first-half possessions, but the defense scored as many points as its offensive counterparts from Texas State.

Up 28-7 at the break, Texas put the game in cruise control in the second half. Texas outscored the Bobcats 21-0 in the third quarter, and Texas State never got any closer than 42 points in the final frame.

Texas transfers make the most of their first games with Longhorns

Smothers finished with 70 rushing yards on 10 carries while turning three receptions into 28 yards and a 13-yard jaunt into the end zone. Meanwhile, Coleman scored on two of his three receptions. Brown added a 21-yard touchdown run after Manning was pulled midway through the third quarter.

Those three weren't the only transfers who had a successful debut with the Longhorns. On defense, linebacker Rasheem Biles intercepted a pass and forced the fumble on which Littleton scored:

WR Sterling Berkhalter: receptions for 26 yards

LB Rasheem Biles (Pitt): 5 tackles, an interception, one forced fumble

RB Raleek Brown (Arizona State) : 11 rushes for 34 yards and 2 TDs

WR Cam Coleman (Auburn): 3 receptions for 70 yards, 2 touchdowns

RB Hollywood Smothers (NC State): 10 rushes for 70 yards; 3 catches for 28 yards, one TD

10 rushes for 70 yards; 3 catches for 28 yards, one TD

K Gianni Spetic ( Memphis ): 1-for-1 FG, 7-for-7 extra points

Texas also started transfers Melvin Siani (Wake Forest) and Dylan Sikorski ( Oregon State ) on the offensive line. Former Western Kentucky guard Laurence Seymore III also received some valuable reps on the offensive line during the first half.

No. 1 Ohio State is the next team up for Texas

In the leadup to the Texas State game, Texas insisted that its focus was on the Bobcats and not the following week's showdown against Ohio State . Texas coach Steve Sarkisian even insisted on the SEC's Wednesday conference call that "I know everyone is wanting to talk about next week, (but) this team we're playing this week, don't be surprised at the end of November if they're not in the talk of making the college football playoff. I think Texas State's a real good team. They've got our attention."

But with the Bobcats beaten, the eyes of Texas now shift to Ohio State. The top-ranked team in both the Associated Press and coaches polls, Ohio State opened its season Saturday with a 56-3 rout of Ball State .

As long as neither team slips in the AP poll, this will mark just the third top-five showdown in the past 25 years at DKR. One of those other marquee matchups was then-No. 1 Ohio State's 24-7 win over then-No. 2 Texas during the second week of the 2006 season.

articles.title: 5 things Penn State proved after dominant Week 1 win vs. Marshall
articles.summary: Penn State proved a lot in its Week 1 win over Marshall. Here are the five major takeaways from the game.
articles.body:
Penn State wanted to get out to a fast start to the season, and that's exactly what happened Saturday afternoon. Things started off shaky when Marshall held the Nittany Lions to a field goal on the first drive of the game, but then the floodgates opened soon after.

They put up 45 points on the day and looked dominant in all three phases at different points of the game. There were a lot of questions for Penn State to answer, and while it didn't play the toughest opponent in the world, this opening game gave a lot of insight into how the team could operate this year.

Let's look at the five biggest takeaways from this high-flying start to the season.

Penn State desperately needed one of its wide receivers to emerge as an impact player, and Koby Howard was the guy on Saturday. Not only did the sophomore have one of the better receiving games in team history — he had one of the best performances of any wideout in the country this week, including Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith.

Howard exploded for 161 yards and a touchdown on just six catches. Whether it was a catch-and-run, a great route to get him wide open, or a jump ball that quarterback Rocco Becht gave him a chance on, the second-year wideout did it all. We'll see what he looks like later in the year against better competition, but Howard looks like a potential star right now.

It doesn't matter what team lines up on the other side of you, shutting out an opponent is difficult at any level of football. But that's exactly what Nittany Lions defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn did, calling as close to a perfect game as humanly possible.

The variety that he displayed on defense was beautiful to watch. Rarely was there ever a typical four-man pass rush — instead Lynn opted to have linebackers frequently lurking around the line of scrimmage and blitzing. This resulted in Thundering Herd quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson running for his life all day, with Penn State picking up two sacks and forcing him out of the pocket much quicker than he wanted to be.

There were no holes in the running game and no space down the field for Marshall to throw into. This is only Week 1, so it's exciting to think of how much room this defense still has to grow.

The special teams unit will be one that flies under the radar for Penn State after such a convincing win. However, its impact could very well be felt later in the year when the margins are closer and teams need every advantage they can get.

The Nittany Lions had a great return to start the season, taking the opening kickoff about 35 yards before a penalty set them up at midfield. Then, they nearly blocked Marshall's first two punts of the day. And the unit's solid showing was capped off by a punt late in the game that was downed at the one-yard line, putting the Thundering Herd in an impossible situation that resulted in an interception by safety Bryson Williams . Don't sleep on the special teams unit — they might come in play against a tougher opponent.

Matt Campbell is known to have a terrible temper, and while Saturday's game didn't offer many moments for anger, he still let the emotions loose a little bit. Cameras showed him screaming on the sidelines a couple times, and that ruggedness showed up in the new Penn State coach's decision making as well.

Campbell decided to kick a field goal on his first fourth-down situation of the game, but went for it twice later on in the game when his team was up big. It isn't indicative of how he will treat every fourth-down call for the rest of the season, but it shows he isn't afraid to roll the dice, even if the situation doesn't call for risk.

Penn State has been far too conservative at times in the past, so this is a welcome change of philosophy if it continues.

The Nittany Lions came into Week 1 with a mixed bag of expectations. Some expected them to improve marginally from last year but take some lumps as the roster gels, while others expected the team to immediately click and make the College Football Playoff .

It's just one game, but it's pretty clear which one of those expectations Penn State is closer to at this point. A lot of other Big Ten teams got favorable matchups to open the season, but not all of them dominated the game the way this team did. It's clear that the roster has impact players on both sides of the ball and a schedule that will allow them to maximize their potential.

There is still a lot of football left to be played, but Penn State made a big statement in Week 1. There's no reason this team can't be a player near the top of the conference when this season is over.

articles.body:
Katie Taylor's career was soaked in blood, tears and triumph.

The Irishwoman has stepped away from the sport aged 40 after 27 fights and 26 wins after a memorable night at Dublin's Croke Park .

Making her amateur debut in 2001, Taylor won every medal and title she could have and more importantly had a lasting effect on women's boxing and women as athletes.

BBC Sport takes a look back on some of the best pictures from her iconic career.

articles.title: Why Beau Peterson couldn't pass up signing with Houston Astros instead of playing at Texas
articles.summary: The high school infielder was set to play for the University of Texas before signing with the Astros, whom he was familiar with since his childhood.
articles.body:
Growing up in the Kansas City area, Beau Peterson was a young Royals fan when the team reached back-to-back World Series in 2014 and '15. During the 2015 playoffs, Peterson said, his family made a trip to Houston to watch the Royals and Astros in the AL Division Series, his first time at then-Minute Maid Park.

Peterson was back in the building Saturday, now a recent Astros draft pick embarking on his professional career. The Astros selected Peterson, an infielder who turned 19 last month, from Mill Valley (Kan.) High School with the No. 133 overall pick in the fourth round of theJuly draft, paying a significantly over-slot bonus to sign him.

The Astros drafted Peterson, who was committed to University of Texas, with the compensation pick they received for Framber Valdez signing elsewhere as a qualified free agent and signed him for a reported $3 million bonus. Slot value for the No. 133 pick this year was $569,600.

Peterson, who attended Saturday's game against Arizona and watched batting practice on the field, said he neared the draft open-minded about taking the college or professional route. But he said the Astros showed steady interest, including a Zoom meeting last winter and contact in the week before the draft.

"We had a strong relationship and we were loyal to Texas and it was going to take a lot not to go there, and Houston came around and you can't pass up this opportunity," Peterson said. "You're playing for so much more than just chasing your dreams. And the goal is to win a World Series and become an All-Star, so the earlier you can start the better and I got that opportunity and can't thank the Lord enough."

Peterson, a left-handed hitter who played shortstop and pitched in high school, had some high-profile accolades on the prep circuit. In 2025, he won the MLB All-Star High School Home Run Derby that was held during All-Star week at Truist Park in Atlanta . He was named Gatorade's Kansas baseball player of the year this spring.

During the draft, Astros director of amateur scouting Cam Pendino said the team views Peterson as "a left-handed premium bat who's got power, he's got a real approach, made contact and performed over the summer." Pendino said the Astros project Peterson as a third baseman. Some third-party evaluators suggested before the draft that Peterson could end up in the corner outfield.

Peterson, who reported to the Astros' minor-league facility in West Palm Beach, Fla., after signing in late July, said he is working primarily at third base with some outfield reps. Peterson had hamate surgery on his right hand after the high school season and so is "just getting my feet back under me," he said. After his visit to Houston, he'll return to West Palm Beach for the start of instructional league camp.

The Astros selected four prep players in this year's draft and signed two - Peterson and third-round pick Keon Johnson, an infielder from Macon (Ga.) First Presbyterian. Peterson said he and Johnson knew each other through the travel ball circuit and are rooming together as they begin their professional journeys in West Palm Beach.

"I heard my name called (in the draft) and it's a dream come true," Peterson said, "and now the work really starts."

articles.title: 'One of the best' - boxing world reacts to Taylor's farewell win
articles.summary: Some of the biggest names in women's boxing pay tribute to Katie Taylor after the Irish great ended her career with victory over Flora Pili at Croke Park.
articles.body:
Some of the biggest names in women's boxing have paid tribute to Katie Taylor after the Irish great ended her career with victory over Flora Pili at Croke Park .

Unified lightweight champion Caroline Dubois called Taylor "one of the best to ever do it", while Claressa Shields said the 40-year-old deserved to "ride off into the sunset".

Taylor beat Pili on points in Dublin to become undisputed light-welterweight champion and retires with 26 wins from 27 professional contests, Olympic gold and three undisputed title triumphs across two divisions.

"Thank you so much for paving the way," Londoner Dubois wrote on X. "Wishing you happiness, success and joy for this next season."

Taylor was sharper throughout, repeatedly beating the Frenchwoman to the punch before finishing with one final burst of combinations as the crowd rose to its feet.

American Shields - the self-proclaimed Greatest Woman of All Time - added: "Congrats Katie. Now ride off into the sunset. You deserve it all."

Super-featherweight champion Alycia Baumgardner described Taylor as "a trailblazer who helped set the stage for all of us".

"What a legacy," she wrote. "It's been a privilege watching your journey from the beginning."

'There will never be another one like her'

Taylor's farewell unfolded in front of more than 80,000 fans in Dublin, with Westlife performing before the main event and Croke Park providing a fitting backdrop to her final night.

Former world champion Carl Frampton said Taylor's relationship with the Irish public was unlike anything else in boxing.

"You can tell that she doesn't enjoy doing stuff in front of the media, but she still has this adulation from everybody," the Northern Irishman said.

"Katie Taylor is different, she's special and there will never be another one like her."

Former cruiserweight world champion Tony Bellew described the occasion as one of the most remarkable exits the sport had seen.

"I don't think in all of my years of watching this game, I have seen an exit as beautiful, amazing and fitting," he said.

"She has just retired as the greatest champion ever. I have never seen a fighter leave as an undisputed champion on their own terms."

Former world champion Barry Jones picked out the final 20 seconds, when Taylor produced the kind of rapid combinations which defined so many of her biggest fights.

"That's what you really remember about her," he said on the Dazn broadcast.

"Those rallies of big punches, combinations and that's how she finished her last fight."

American Mikaela Mayer - who was also ringside - was struck by the final image of Taylor placing her gloves in the centre of the ring.

"I was sitting there watching her put her gloves in the centre of the ring and it's like a story," she said.

Taylor had long dreamed of fighting at Croke Park and had made clear she wanted the stadium to stage the final chapter of her career.

Bellew said there was "no way" Taylor would return to boxing, although he could see her remaining involved by mentoring younger fighters.

"She will always be there to give her advice, speak to her and help her," he said.

"But ultimately she will sail off into the sunset and who could possibly deserve it more."

articles.title: Conforto homers, Hoerner has 3 hits to lead the Cubs past the Marlins, 6-5
articles.summary: Michael Conforto homered and singled, Nico Hoerner had three hits and an RBI and the Chicago Cubs beat the Miami Marlins 6-5 on Saturday.  Michael Busch and...
articles.body:
MIAMI (AP) — Michael Conforto homered and singled, Nico Hoerner had three hits and an RBI and the Chicago Cubs beat the Miami Marlins 6-5 on Saturday.

Michael Busch and Miguel Amaya each doubled and singled for the Cubs, who finished with 13 hits. Cubs star outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong singled, walked and drove in a run, while Ian Happ had two hits and two RBIs.

Kyle Stowers and Griffin Conine homered for two of the Marlins' six hits.

Ryan Rolison (8-1) got the final out in the seventh and first in the eighth for the win. Ryan Zeferjahn pitched the last 1 2/3 innings for his fifth save. After a 3-2 called third strike with two out to Conine in the ninth was overturned on the ABS review, Zeferjahn retired Otto Lopez on a flyout to right.

Cubs starter Javier Assad allowed three runs and three hits over 4 2/3 innings. Recalled from Triple-A Saturday, Assad walked five and struck out three.

Caleb Thielbar relieved Assad with a runner on in the fifth and allowed Conine's drive into the upper deck in right that got Miami within 5-4.

Busch singled in a run in the sixth to make it 6-4 before Miami narrowed it to one again on Stowers' solo homer in the seventh.

Conforto's solo homer and Happ's two-run single in the third off Marlins starter Ryan Gusto (1-4) in the third put the Cubs ahead 3-0.

Chicago padded the lead on Crow-Armstrong's RBI single in the fourth.

The Cubs have not announced a starter for the series finale Sunday, while RHP Tyler Phillips (4-6, 3.43) was set to start for the Marlins.

articles.title: David Beckham’s ‘fierce temper’ and hidden side exposed as new biography examines his billionaire empire
articles.summary: International Sports News: David Beckham’s public image has long leaned toward the charming football star, while Victoria Beckham has often been portrayed as the more intimidati.
articles.body: David Beckham’s public image has long leaned toward the charming football star, while Victoria Beckham has often been portrayed as the more intimidating half of the marriage. A new biography challenges that familiar picture, offering a different look at the couple’s personalities, ambitions and business strategy. Author Alison Boshoff says her reporting over nearly three decades led her to rethink what she thought she knew about one of Britain’s most famous couples.David Beckham’s business ambition helped shape Brand BeckhamAccording to Boshoff, the biggest surprise while researching Brand Beckham was how different David and Victoria appeared from their long-standing public images.Victoria, she says, is far more sensitive and insecure than her carefully controlled public persona might suggest. David, meanwhile, comes across as considerably tougher and more determined behind closed doors.Boshoff described Beckham as “a hundred percent in charge” and said he has “quite a fierce temper.”That portrayal adds another layer to the former England captain’s remarkable transformation from football superstar to global businessman.David was already one of the most recognizable athletes in the world when his playing career gave him a platform few others could match. Rather than relying solely on sporting fame, however, he wanted to turn that attention into lasting wealth.Boshoff says he worked with Simon Fuller, the manager who had also represented Victoria, to build what became known as Brand Beckham. The strategy allowed David to move beyond football and establish commercial partnerships, investments and ventures that could continue long after his playing days ended.That long-term thinking appears to have paid off. Forbes has included Beckham among the small group of sportspeople who have reached billionaire status, while the Sunday Times Rich List has placed the combined Beckham fortune at around £1.2 billion.The numbers help explain why the couple remain such a powerful celebrity brand. Their fame is no longer tied to one sport, one fashion label or one generation of fans.Beckham family feud has not weakened the brandPerhaps the most unexpected part of Boshoff’s assessment concerns the recent tensions surrounding the Beckham family.Celebrity scandals often threaten carefully built reputations. In the Beckham case, Boshoff believes the intense public interest has produced almost the opposite effect.The family drama has kept David and Victoria in headlines, creating another wave of attention around their personal lives and businesses. Boshoff argues that curiosity surrounding the fallout has increased interest in Beckham-linked products rather than turning consumers away.She points to David’s commercial relationships, including his Stella Artois campaign and his health and wellness products, as examples of businesses that can benefit from his enormous visibility.That does not mean controversy is automatically good for every celebrity. The Beckham story is unusual because the family already has decades of public recognition, a broad commercial portfolio and a loyal global audience.Their ability to remain relevant across football, fashion, entertainment and business gives the brand considerable staying power.For Boshoff, that is perhaps the strangest lesson from covering the Beckhams for so long. The couple’s public image may keep changing, but the business machine built around their names appears remarkably resilient.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 8 months, Moscow-to-Munich flights, but now he is 'fed up': Behind Russia No. 1 Ian Nepomniachtchi's tattoos
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: The word “tattoo” is believed to have come from Polynesian languages, particularly words such as \"tatau\", a term associated with traditiona.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The word “tattoo” is believed to have come from Polynesian languages, particularly words such as "tatau", a term associated with traditional body art in that region. European sailors encountered Polynesian tattooing and helped carry the word back into European languages. Even thousands of years earlier, ancient Egyptians were already tattooing their bodies, with some of the earliest known examples found on female mummies. Researchers suggest that their markings may have served social, ritual or protective purposes.Millennia later, tattoos still carry stories. On the arms of Russia’s top-ranked chess grandmaster Ian Nepomniachtchi, they surely do.A two-time back-to-back winner of the prestigious Candidates Tournament, Nepomniachtchi, affectionately known in the chess world simply as "Nepo", was initially slated to fly from Moscow to Bengaluru on September 2 for the Global Chess League (GCL).Opting to delay his travel, he touched down on the morning of September 4, a day before the start of the tournament. The late arrival has effectively cost him any chance for local sightseeing, but the city has still managed to win him over."I really like the climate; it's very mild compared to what I'm used to in India when I visited previously. And yeah, the place is very nice," Nepo told TimesofIndia.com with a smile during an exclusive interaction as his team, Ganges Grandmasters, opened their GCL campaign with a victory on Saturday.Whether you were inside the arena or watching from a screen, Nepomniachtchi’s arms were hard to miss. At a glance, they looked less like a grandmaster’s limbs and more like a vivid canvas, covered in colours and intricate artwork that stood out against the otherwise restrained setting of professional chess.The elite circuit is a world of pristine blazers, pressed shirts and strict sartorial codes, where body art is rarely part of the picture. Here, at GCL, that is not the case."Normally, it's not approved by the dress code. So, this is only for a gym," Nepo admitted, laughing as he rolled back his sleeves to reveal his tattoo.When asked how many he has. "Not that much, only two," he replied. On his right arm carries a powerful mantra. “Rise and rise again and again like the Phoenix from the ashes; until the lambs have become lions.”"I have this one, but this comes from 2023. I think I played the first GCL right after getting this," he explained. "I like this quote. This I wanted to get many, many years before. It's always hard to make a decision to get something onto your skin."The process for his right arm was surprisingly painless, which gave the grandmaster a false sense of security."This one felt so easy," Nepo recalled. "So, I felt, alright, maybe the full-sleeve is fine. Why not?"A test of patience off the boardThat casual "why not" evolved into an agonising, transatlantic project on his left arm that would test his endurance on another level."My nickname is Lachesis, and it's the Greek goddess of fate," he told this website, referencing his popular social media handle, lachesisq. "I wanted a Greek goddess, and it took me some time to find a master, an artist who specialises (in this)."Nepo eventually found the right artist, but that artist was in Germany."The artist I was working with is based in Munich," he revealed. "It was logistically a bit tricky as I live in Moscow. We completed several sessions, and eventually, it was eight sessions total starting from September and ending in April."The resulting full-sleeve is what one can call a chef-d'œuvre. "Eventually, it's a mix of ideas," the Russian grandmaster stated while examining the ink. "You have some snake for Ouroboros and also some chess pieces for whatever reason, but it was an idea from my artist, and I didn't really argue."But for the 36-year-old Nepo, it was a classic case of no pain, no gain."This one (right arm) was completely painless, and this (left arm) was a hell of a time," he confessed. "I finished it (the left one) this year, but it's a full sleeve. It was quite painful, to be honest, and it took a while. So, for now, I'm fed up with pain. I was patient; I tolerated a lot."Read Also: 'Gukesh's lifetime dream just came too early': American GM Levon Aronian assesses Sindarov clash | ExclusiveNow that the suffering has ended with its completion, he doesn't plan on returning to the tattoo chair anytime soon. Now, he just hopes that people can see, and understand, the meaning behind the artwork."And this is supposed to be a phoenix," he said with a final grin, gesturing to his right arm, "if it's recognisable or not."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Oregon rallies from slow start, thwarts Boise State's upset bid in season opener
articles.summary: Dante Moore threw for 388 yards and three touchdowns as No. 2 Oregon rallied past Boise State in a tense 34-27 season opener at Autzen Stadium.
articles.body: No. 2 Oregon survived a scare in its first game of the 2026 college football season Saturday. Despite entering the opener as heavy favorites over unranked Boise State, the Ducks found themselves tied 27-27 in the fourth quarter. But the Ducks ultimately held off a resilient Broncos team when wide receiver Dakorien Moore hauled in a 62-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Dante Moore, putting Oregon ahead for good. The Broncos, who join the rebuilt Pac-12 Conference this year, went 9-5 last season in the Mountain West. The Ducks tied it on Jordon Davison’s 1-yard dive early in the second quarter. After Evan Stewart muffed a punt and the Broncos recovered, Sire Gaines scored on a 37-yard reception to give Boise State the lead again. articles.title: “We’re excited to impact more”: How Vanessa Trump quietly supported Tiger Woods as his $50M TGR Foundation mission reached more young lives
articles.summary: International Sports News: Tiger Woods and Vanessa Trump shared two notable moments around the golfer’s charity work in early 2026. Vanessa joined Woods for his 50th birthday ce.
articles.body: Tiger Woods and Vanessa Trump shared two notable moments around the golfer’s charity work in early 2026. Vanessa joined Woods for his 50th birthday celebration at The Breakers in Palm Beach on January 14, an event that also highlighted the growing impact of his TGR Foundation. The foundation announced that it had raised more than $50 million for its education initiatives.Weeks later, Vanessa again appeared connected to the same cause, this time in a much quieter way. Woods marked the 20th anniversary of his TGR Learning Lab in Anaheim, while Vanessa showed support for a post from the official learning lab account featuring Woods and students. She did not claim a role in the fundraising, but her presence and online gesture linked her to an important part of Woods’ community work.Vanessa Trump joined Tiger Woods as his charity work reached a major milestoneWoods’ January 14 celebration carried more weight than a traditional birthday party. The event at The Breakers brought together around 300 guests and also served as a major gathering for the TGR Foundation during its 30th anniversary year. Vanessa attended alongside her daughter, Kai Trump, while Jon Bon Jovi performed during the evening.The bigger story, however, was happening around Woods’ foundation. TGR Foundation announced that it had raised more than $50 million to support its education mission and expand its programs into communities that need greater access to opportunities. The fundraising total included a separate $20 million pledge from the Arthur M. Blank Family Foundation for a new TGR Learning Lab in Atlanta.That distinction is important because there is no evidence that Vanessa personally donated to the $50 million total. Her connection to the night came through her attendance and her presence alongside Woods as he celebrated a milestone that went far beyond golf.In a statement released after the January 14 event, Woods explained why the foundation’s work had become such an important part of his legacy.“Tonight was a reminder that the legacy I’m most proud of isn’t on the golf course; it’s the work we’ve done to positively impact the lives of students through TGR Foundation.”He also made it clear that the next stage of the foundation’s work would focus on reaching even more young people.“I am excited for what’s next as we expand alongside our great supporters to reach more young people from communities in need.”That message became even more relevant when Woods later returned to one of the foundation’s most important projects. Vanessa Trump quietly backed Tiger Woods as he celebrated the TGR Learning Lab’s impactOn February 11, Woods turned the spotlight toward Anaheim and the TGR Learning Lab, the education project that has been central to his foundation’s community work. He shared photos with students and faculty on Instagram while reflecting on the 20th anniversary of the facility.In the caption, Woods explained why the project had personal meaning to him.“After 9/11, I wanted to create a safe space for kids to learn, grow and chase after their dreams.”Woods then pointed to how far the project has come since the Anaheim facility opened in February 2006. He said TGR Foundation had served more than 217,000 children through its TGR Learning Labs and added that “we’re excited to impact more students from communities in need.”That final message also ties directly back to what Woods said after the January fundraiser. His focus was no longer simply on celebrating what the foundation had already accomplished. He was talking about expanding its reach.The Anaheim lab has a particularly personal connection to Woods. He opened the 35,000-square-foot facility in 2006 near H.G. “Dad” Miller Golf Course, where he practiced as a teenager. The program provides students with opportunities involving STEAM education, health and wellness, college preparation and career exploration.Vanessa was not featured in Woods’ Instagram post and did not leave a comment under it.
