articles.title: Michigan Wolverines fend off shocking upset bid from Western Michigan in early season thriller
articles.summary: Michigan football nearly relived its Appalachian State nightmare as Western Michigan led 12-7 before Bryce Underwood's 46-yard Hail Mary saved the day.
articles.body: We just passed the 19th anniversary of Michigan's shocking upset loss to Appalachian State that opened their 2007 season. Well, we came about as close as you can to another major Michigan upset to kick off this year. The Wolverines got their slate underway on Saturday night at Michigan Stadium by welcoming the Western Michigan Broncos. THE 2007 MOUNTAINEERS REMAIN COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S GREATEST 'WHAT-IF' STORY NEARLY TWO DECADES LATER As is often the case in these Week 1 matchups, Michigan came into this one as an overwhelming 27.5-point favorite. Oddsmakers were also looking at a fairly high-scoring game with the o/u set at 49.5. However, this turned into a low-scoring, defensive battle, with Michigan opening the scoring when QB Bryce Underwood punched it into the end zone from the 1-yard line. A few minutes later, the Broncos answered with a field goal, then tacked on another before halftime, and that was the end of the scoring in the first half. OREGON RALLIES FROM SLOW START, THWARTS BOISE STATE'S UPSET BID IN SEASON OPENER The teams went to the locker room with Michigan up just 7-6. That was a stunner, but surely Michigan would come out firing and put the 2025 MAC champions away. Nope. The next time either team would score wasn't until the fourth quarter, when Western Michigan kicked their third field goal of the game to go up 9-7. Both teams failed to score on their next drives, but with Michigan looking like they were on the verge of at least marching downfield for a late game-winning field goal, the Broncos pulled off a stunner. Western Michigan's Joshua Franklin managed to punch the ball out of Underwood's grasp as he fell to the turf, with the Broncos pouncing on top of it. DEION SANDERS TAKES MULTIPLE SWIPES AT HIS CRITICS AFTER COLORADO STUNS GEORGIA TECH Despite a scare due to a fumble of their own, the Broncos hung on to the ball and added another field goal to go up 12-7. On the ensuing drive, Underwood connected with receiver Channing Goodwin around midfield, and with no timeouts, the Wolverines scrambled to the line of scrimmage to spike the ball with just nine seconds on the clock. On the final play of the game, Underwood found space and gave his receivers time to get downfield before heaving a bomb that ended up sailing just out the back of the end zone. But Michigan caught a break. Upon review, it was found that there was still one second left on the clock. It was a controversial call, to say the least. Prepare to hear plenty of talk about it this week. The decision left just enough time for the Wolverines to get a snap off, with Underwood connecting with JJ Buchanan for a touchdown and a 13-12 Michigan win. That 46-yard beauty of a Hail Mary for the win was the last of Underwood's 170 passing yards. He also rushed for 46 yards and one touchdown. That's a maiden win for the Kyle Whittingham era in Ann Arbor, and surely no one saw it looking like that. A heartbreaker for the Broncos and a heart-stopper for Michigan. We're barely into the college football season, and we already have a classic (with a bit of controversy mixed in to boot). CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Things will not get any easier for the Wolverines, as their next game will be on Sept. 12 when they welcome the No. 10 Oklahoma Sooners to the Big House.

articles.title: Clock controversy hangs over Michigan’s last-second Hail Mary in season opening win
articles.summary: Given an unlikely second chance at a game-ending Hail Mary, Bryce Underwood connected with JJ Buchanan for a 47-yard touchdown pass that lifted No. 16 Michigan over Western Michigan 13-12 on Saturday night.
articles.body: Given an unlikely second chance at a game-ending Hail Mary, Bryce Underwood connected with JJ Buchanan for a 47-yard touchdown pass that lifted No. 16 Michigan over Western Michigan 13-12 on Saturday night. The Wolverines were 27 1/2-point favorites in coach Kyle Whittingham’s debut. The Broncos thought they’d secured a historic upset when Underwood’s first Hail Mary sailed out of bounds with the clock expired. WMU players were already on the field celebrating when officials called for a review. TV replays showed the clock hitting zero before the ball hit the hands of a Western Michigan defender, but officials ruled there was a second still to play. “I was pretty sure there was 1 second left,” Whittingham said. Underwood heaved another throw, and Buchanan leaped to snag it and came down with it in the end zone. “One for the history books right here,” Whittingham said. Western Michigan was threatening to hand Michigan perhaps its biggest upset since a season-opening loss to Appalachian State in 2007, when the Wolverines were 33-point favorites. The Broncos kicked four field goals and forced three turnovers, including a late fumble by Underwood. WMU went ahead for the first time early in the fourth quarter on Dieter Kelly’s 39-yard field goal that capped a 20-play drive that took 13:40 off the clock. Underwood lost a fumble at his 31 with 1:50 left after throwing an interception in the first half and nearly getting picked off two more times. “There was not hooting and hollering in the locker room because we have a lot of work to do,” Whittingham said. Kelly, a junior-college transfer from College of San Mateo, made his fourth field goal with 35 seconds left to force the Wolverines to score a touchdown to win — and they did in dramatic fashion. Western Michigan, which has played major college football since 1962 in the Mid-American Conference, has never beaten an opponent in the top 20 of the Associated Press poll. The takeaway Western Michigan: The defending MAC champions were able to retain key players, keeping them out of the transfer portal, and will be contenders to repeat. Michigan: Underwood started strong with a touchdown drive and finished it well, but made a lot of mistakes in between. “This isn’t on Bryce Underwood,” Whittingham said. “It’s on me.” Up next Western Michigan hosts Monmouth on Saturday. Michigan hosts No. 10 Oklahoma on Saturday.

articles.title: Haudenschild and Nordstrom hustle to Huset’s Shootout
articles.summary: BRANDON, S.D. (HUSETS) – Sheldon Haudenschild and Lance Nordstrom delivered winning performances on Friday at Huset’s Speedway, which hosted the opening roun...
articles.body:
BRANDON, S.D. (HUSETS) – Sheldon Haudenschild and Lance Nordstrom delivered winning performances on Friday at Huset's Speedway, which hosted the opening round of the L.G. Everist Huset's Shootout presented by D & I Railroad.

Additionally, Craig Hanisch captured the Nordstrom's Automotive Late Model Street Stocks track championship.

The $15,000-to-win World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series main event got off to a rough start with a red flag on Lap 1 and caution on Lap 3 for a multiple-car incident. It didn't take long to heat up as Sheldon Haudenschild drove around Garet Williamson, who led the first 11 circuits, in turns three and four on Lap 12. Williamson briefly reclaimed the lead in turns one and two before Haudenschild powered into the top spot exiting turn two.

Two laps later, Williamson once again used a slide job to take the lead for a few feet before Haudenschild rocketed back by off turn four.

A caution on Lap 16 was followed by a close call on Lap 18 for Haudenschild, who squeezed between a stopped car near the top of turn two and the wall, appearing to tag the outside wall during the dicey maneuver.

"Man, that first one got my heartrate up big time," he said. "I thought I was done. It's tough to see around that corner. He was yelling red (on the RACEceiver) and you know I'm sliding up the track. I'd rather hit the wall than him."

Haudenschild was hard on the brakes during another close call to avoid a stopped car on the backstretch on Lap 22. Meanwhile, Michael "Buddy" Kofoid used the mid-race cautions and restarts to drive into the second position by Lap 19.

The final 14 laps didn't see a caution and Haudenschild was able to maintain a comfortable lead despite racing through traffic the final seven laps. His margin of victory was 0.527 seconds.

"What a gnarly race," he said after his ninth World of Outlaws triumph of the season and second at Huset's Speedway this year. "This heat was no joke today. Thank you to the fans that stuck that one out cause that was a hot one. Good to get a win early in the week here."

Williamson used a last-lap pass to garner the runner-up result.

"You're a sitting duck out there in traffic," he said. "Sheldon got by us there and then I feel we ran back to him in traffic. I think we went back and forth a lap or two. Buddy got by and then kinda just paced him, started searching a little bit. That's when we really got good. Our car was phenomenal all night so that was really good."

Kofoid's third-place showing marked his fourth podium in the sixth World of Outlaws race at Huset's Speedway this season.

"Just restarts and maneuverability," he said of his strengths. "I got to the top at the right time and had good restarts where I could fire off on the outside. I felt really good on restarts and on short runs especially."

World of Outlaws points leader David Gravel ran fourth and Carson Macedo placed fifth.

Gravel set quick time during qualifying for the fourth straight World of Outlaws race. Gravel, Logan Schuchart, Haudenschild and Williamson posted heat race wins. Williamson topped the dash and Cole Macedo was the Last Chance Showdown winner.

Nordstrom led the distance of the 18-lap Nordstrom's Automotive Late Model Street Stocks main event for his first career triumph at the track.

"Oh, this is something I've wanted to do my whole life," he said. "It's a pretty cool experience."

The final 16 laps ran non-stop after the lone caution of the race occurred on Lap 3. Nordstrom held off runner-up finisher Aaron Foote by 1.150 seconds with Trevor Tesch rounding out the podium. Chris Ellingson finished fourth and Matt Steuerwald was fifth.

Hanisch, who placed eighth in the race, unofficially finished four points ahead of Garet Deboer for the track title. It's his third total championship at Huset's Speedway.

"It's a good track," he said. "It's changed over the years since I've been here."

The heat races were won by Ron Howe and Nordstrom.

The L.G. Everist Huset's Shootout resumes on Saturday as Round 2 is presented by Ace Ready Mix. The finale on Sunday is presented by Myrl & Roy's Paving. Each night showcases the World of Outlaws with 600cc Winged Micro Sprints part of Saturday's program.

The main gates open at 4 p.m. with hot laps at 6:30 p.m. each night.

articles.title: Josh Sargent scores first Toronto FC hat trick in wild draw
articles.summary: By Alex CalabreseTORONTO – Josh Sargent is playing like a man on a mission.Toronto FC's marquee 2026 signing delivered his biggest performance to date on Sat...
articles.body:
TORONTO – Josh Sargent is playing like a man on a mission.

Toronto FC 's marquee 2026 signing delivered his biggest performance to date on Saturday, scoring a first career hat trick in a wild 4-4 draw against Chicago Fire FC at BMO Field.

"It's been a while, so happy to finally get my first professional hat trick," Sargent said postgame.

"My kids have been waiting for this moment. They've been pestering me, saying, 'You gonna score today? You gonna score today?' So I'm very happy about it, of course."

Sargent, who joined Toronto over the winter from EFL Championship side Norwich City in a transfer worth up to a reported $27 million, is storming into form as his new team climbs up the Eastern Conference standings.

With 4g/1a in his last four games, the 26-year-old has helped the Reds go undefeated in six (two wins, four draws) to move within a point of an Audi MLS Cup Playoffs spot.

"I've been saying all along, I think Josh is absolutely fantastic," head coach Robin Fraser said. "I hear questions like, 'What's wrong with him? What does Josh need to do to get off the mark?' I think he's tremendous.

"I think he's tremendous not only because of his goal-scoring ability, [but] his willingness to work for the team. I think you saw so much of what Josh brings to us tonight, not just in the three goals, but the work that he did outside of it."

Since arriving in MLS, Sargent seems to have a knack for scoring against the Fire and former USMNT head coach Gregg Berhalter.

The Missourian scored at Soldier Field in TFC's final game before the FIFA World Cup . And after outdueling legendary Polish striker Robert Lewandowski - who had 1g/1a for the visitors on Saturday - with his first-ever hat trick, more than half of Sargent's seven league goals have come against Chicago

Now, with Toronto pushing for an Audi MLS Cup Playoff spot, getting their marquee man in the best possible form is priority No. 1.

"I'm naturally a very hard worker, and days like this, where I feel like all my hard work kind of pays off, it's very gratifying," Sargent said.

"I have a process, and if I keep doing the same things, keep trying to put myself in the right spots, the goals will come. So that's what happened today."

articles.title: Lane Kiffin roasts Clemson with LSU leading by 28: 'Imagine if we had pro players'
articles.summary: In a halftime interview with ESPN, and with his team up on Clemson by 28, Lane Kiffin said 'imagine if we had pro players' when discussing the lead
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin had little reason to be upset at halftime of his first game as LSU 's football coach, with the Tigers beating Clemson by 28, but before he went back to the locker room, he had one more thing he wanted to say to the millions of fans tuning in.

At the end of his halftime interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe, and as he was walking away from the camera, Kiffin turned around to deliver a final message.

"It took everything not to say 'Imagine if we had pro players,'" Kiffin said before running off to the tunnel at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

For the past several weeks, Kiffin has occupied a familiar role as one of college football's villains, as two of his former players at Mississippi — tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris — have fought to become eligible to play for LSU this season after signing NFL contracts earlier this year.

The two were part of a lawsuit that ended with a Louisiana judge granting a temporary restraining order and opening the door for them to commit to Kiffin, their coach at Ole Miss before he left for LSU after the 2025 regular season. Even after the SEC passed a rule prohibiting former professional players from playing at member schools, a Louisiana judge approved a preliminary injunction on Thursday, Sept. 3 that prohibits the SEC and NCAA from punishing schools for suiting up ex-pros.

LSU dominates Clemson without pro players

Despite the favorable court ruling, Kiffin did not add Wright and Harris to the Tigers' roster for their season-opener, though it's possible he could do so for games later this season (even as soon as next week's matchup against Louisiana Tech).

"That wasn't easy. As much as I feel for the players, and I believe that you fight for what you believe in, and I believe that these kids have an opportunity to play, just like all the other kids around the country who are winning court cases and being put on rosters," Kiffin said during an appearance on "College GameDay" on Saturday . "But at the same time, I'm the head coach of LSU and I had to make a decision that is for the big picture for LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could have come by adding them to the roster."

Even without those two, neither of whom were projected to start, LSU was leading Clemson, 31-3, at halftime and were outgaining coach Dabo Swinney's Tigers by a 336-54 margin. The score was that lopsided despite an LSU opening-drive interception that gave Clemson a short field and, ultimately, a field goal and a missed 48-yard LSU field goal in the second quarter.

"We'll go in and we'll make adjustments," he said to Rowe. "We've got to play better in the second half. We can't give away something like the first turnover, man. This should be 38-0."

articles.summary: Scott Abell became the first Rice coach in 30-plus years to win his first two season openers as the Owls cruised past Houston Christian in the crosscity foes...
articles.body:
Rice and Houston Christian met on the football field for the first time Saturday. The matchup seemed to favor the Owls over the Huskies , an FCS institution and member of the Southland Conference.

As expected, Rice proved to be the better team, opening its 2026 season on a high note. After spotting the Huskies three points, the Owls prevailed 31-3 at Rice Stadium.

The Owls were not flashy and HCU's solid defense kept Rice from breaking off many long gainers, limiting the Owls to 28 passing yards in Rice's run-first offense.

Scott Abell become the eighth Owls head coach to win his first two season openers and the first since Fred Goldsmith, who won 35-6 in 1989 at SMU in his debut as a head coach, and then beat Wake Forest 33-17 at home the following season.

Houston Christian came in off a big victory in its opener, a 34-28 upset on the road over nationally ranked Southeastern Louisiana in a league game.

But the Huskies could not stay with the Owls, who pretty much leaned on the ground attack, rushing for 465 of their 487 yards.

Quinton Jackson scored on runs of 12 and 7 yards. D'Andre Hardeman scored the Owls' first touchdown, a 2 yarder. Enock Gota was successful on a 26-yard field goal.

For HCU, Lukasz Smolen's 42-yard field goal midway of the first quarter was HCU's only lead and score.

Kickoff was pushed back 20 minutes from a scheduled 6 p.m. start due to lightning in the area around Rice Stadium.

Jacurri Brown became the ninth different Rice player to start the season opener at quarterback over the past 11 seasons.

Only Wiley Green has made multiple starts at that position in that time period. Green made starts in openers in 2022 (at USC), 2021 (at Arkansas ) and 2019 (at Army). Chase Jenkins made the start at quarterback for the Owls' 2025 opener (at Louisiana).

For the Owls, Tyvonn Byars ran for 104 yards. Brown totaled 98 yards on the ground and Hardeman added 77. Jackson ran for 67.

A transfer from UCF , Brown's biggest gain was a 32-yard run to the left side midway through the third quarter.

Rice turned the ball over on downs near midfield on its opening possession. But the Owls scored a pair of touchdowns and a field goal on their following three drives en route to a 17-3 lead at the break.

HCU totaled 244 yards, mostly under the direction of quarterback Cutter Stewart, who engineered the Huskies' opening win at Southeastern Louisiana.

articles.title: How Michigan Hail Mary changed fortunes of Bryce Underwood, Kyle Whittingham in one second
articles.summary: Bryce Underwood goes from goat to hero on final pass.
articles.body:
Michigan was supposed to re-establish an aura of stability with the arrival of veteran coach Kyle Whittingham in 2026.

In a round-about way, that might have been exactly what happened.

But first, there was dysfunction and controversy – a different breed than what has followed the program for the last five years off the field. A wild finish in Whittingham's debut that – right or wrong – will live on the montages forever at Michigan Stadium.

This all happened in one second that should not have been on the clock in the first place. In a stunning reversal of the "Miracle at Michigan," quarterback Bryce Underwood hit JJ Buchanan on a 47-yard Hail Mary that gave the Wolverines a 13-12 victory against Mid-American Conference preseason favorite Western Michigan.

Time appeared to expire on the previous play – when Underwood's first Hail Mary attempt sailed out of the end zone. Western Michigan players stormed the field. Yet an official review put one second left on the clock. It's as dysfunctional as it sounds.

"Fortunately we had one second left on the clock," Whittingham said on the NBC telecast afterward. "Bryce threw a perfect ball, JJ made a great catch and it's one for the history books right here."

Instead of an addendum to another upset loss between the 34-31 loss to Appalachian State in 2007 under coach Lloyd Carr and the 13-10 loss to Toledo under Rich Rodriguez in 2008 – the Wolverines escaped with a victory ahead of a Week 2 showdown against No. 10 Oklahoma.

Underwood – who finished 12 of 22 for 170 yards, a touchdown and an interception – played the role of hero. Whittingham won his debut with the Wolverines. The Wolverines' all-maize uniforms went from retired attire to remembered forever.

Who knew one second could change those fortunes so fast?

Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary saves rough night

Underwood – the embattled five-star quarterback who struggled as a freshman – hit 5 of 5 passes for 61 yards and scored on a one-yard TD sneak with 9:40 left in the first quarter.

Everything afterward until that final second was brutal. Michigan could not run the ball with Jordan Marshall, who had 11 carries for 44 yards; or freshman Savion Hiter, who had five catches for 15 yards.

The Wolverines were 3 of 10 on third down. Underwood threw an interception late in the first half that set up a Western Michigan field goal and had a fumble on the next-to last drive on a scramble. The Broncos led 12-7 with 35 seconds remaining. The new-look offense under coordinator Jason Beck had a bad night.

For Underwood, a loss would have meant disaster. There were – and still might be – calls to get a look at backup Tommy Carr – the grandson of Lloyd Carr, who won a national championship with the Wolverines in 1997. Underwood had not lived up to the lucrative NIL deal that led him to flip from LSU to Michigan.

Instead, Underwood changed the narrative with that one throw to Buchanan, a slot receiver who made a leaping catch between Western Michigan defenders inside the goal line for the game-winning score.

"Hail to the Victors" played. Michigan students stormed the field against a MAC school.

Kyle Whittingham wins wild Michigan debut

Whittingham knows about spoiling Michigan coaching debuts. He led Utah to victories against the Wolverines in 2007 in Rich Rodriguez's debut and against Jim Harbaugh in 2015.

It was a different game on the other side. The Wolverines were disjointed. Michigan had nine penalties for 80 yards. The Broncos took a 9-7 lead in the fourth quarter on a 20-play, 71-yard drive behind quarterback Broc Lowry that ended with 13:40 left in the fourth quarter.

Western Michigan – led by coach Lance Taylor – outplayed the Wolverines up until the final second. Yet Whittingham's reaction afterward was telling. He's the even-keeled 66-year-old coach who was supposed to bring stability back to Ann Arbor and seemingly built to handle the theatrics that come with coaching at Michigan.

The Wolverines might drop in the AP Poll despite beating Western Michigan, and the controversy around that final second will linger. Michigan still has a tough schedule, and they did not look the part of a Big Ten or College Football Playoff contender. That is reality.

Yet that one second suspended reality in the moment.

Think about what that one second represents. A loss would have been a total embarrassment for the Wolverines.

This would have been the hammer that never dropped with the NCAA investigation into the sign-stealing scandal involving Conor Stallions at the end of the Harbaugh era during the 2023 national championship season. This could have been labeled as a side effect of the dysfunction after Sherrone Moore was fired at the end of the 2024 season and athletic director Warde Manuel stepped down this summer.

Yet you can't put an asterisk next to this victory either. Michigan got away with it again – and Whittingham avoided the fate of some of those wild finishes in Ann Arbor in the past – the ones that always went against the Wolverines.

Kordell Stewart. Cory Lynch. Jalen Watts-Jackson. Those are names that live in Michigan infamy.

Yet this resembled another lesser-replayed finish on Aug. 26, 1995. That is when Scott Dreisbach hit Mercury Hayes for a touchdown in the back corner of the same end zone for an 18-yard TD pass as time expired. That gave Michigan an 18-17 victory against Virginia in Carr's debut – and with it a mostly stable era followed until that Appalachian State upset.

Maybe that identity is back, after all. No matter what, the beginning of the Whittingham era will be defined by that one second.

articles.title: Brooks Nader Goes Viral Twice in One Day at LSU as Baton Rouge Turns Into a Celebrity Circus
articles.summary: College football saw one of its big stories Saturday without having a single snap of football played by Model Brooks Nader. Nader, a former Sports Illustrate...
articles.body:
College football saw one of its big stories Saturday without having a single snap of football played by Model Brooks Nader.

Nader, a former Sports Illustrated Swimsuit model from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, appeared on ESPN's College GameDay. She appeared on screen holding a drink and wearing a tiger-striped corset top with her name on it, on a crowded stage. Promoting the energy drink Celsius, the clip quickly spread across social media.

Just a few hours later, she went viral once more.

The new LSU coach Lane Kiffin walked down Victory Hill for his first game as a coach of the Tigers with Model Brooks Nader, retired LSU gymnast Livvy Dunne, and comedian and podcaster Theo Von walking next to him. On3's Wilson Alexander captured the scene and shared it widely online.

The online reaction was quick. While one post from the Brandon Walker College Football Show called Kiffin the baddest man in college football, another one said the entrance was the trending moment. Some voices disagreed, though. In a Yahoo Sports column, the entrance was called corny, and the columnist said LSU was inviting the circus by hiring Lane Kiffin. At 29 years old, Nader won the Sports Illustrated Swim Search in 2019 and appeared in SI in 2020, 2021, and 2022, becoming a cover model in 2023.

Her connection to LSU runs in the family. Nader's grandfather, Sam Nader, was one of LSU's longest-serving football staffers. Nader has already gone viral at Tiger Stadium, particularly when LSU defeated Alabama in 2022.

Dunne is also familiar to the Baton Rouge crowd. The LSU gymnast played for LSU's women's team, which won the 2024 national championship, and became one of the country's most popular college athletes. LSU officials noted that the game against Clemson has been the largest media and celebrity coverage in Tiger Stadium history. Built in 1924, Tiger Stadium has a long history as one of the oldest active football stadiums.

The night also saw the 500th College GameDay road show. Country artist Lainey Wilson appeared on the pre-game show dressed up in Tigers gear. Speaking about all the attention on Saturday's broadcast, Lane Kiffin said he told his team to stay focused and not to listen to any noise because doing great things always brings hate. He became LSU's coach after a six-year stint at Ole Miss.

Juventus vs AC Milan – Match preview and team news

Further compounding their long-term woes, midfielder Khéphren Thuram is out for several months with a serious injury and has been entirely omitted from the club's 25-man Serie A roster.

Defender Juan Cabal and young forward Jeff Ekhator also remain out with long-term issues.

For this specific matchday, short-term setbacks rule out fullback Andrea Cambiaso, who sustained an ankle sprain against Parma, while Weston McKennie is training separately.

Deadline-day midfield signing Pape Matar Sarr is also unavailable due to a muscle problem, forcing tactical adjustments.

AC Milan travels to the Allianz Stadium boasting a virtually full-strength squad, presenting manager Rubén Amorim with plenty of tactical flexibility.

While Fikayo Tomori has returned to the team after his anticipated transfer-window move did not materialise, he is still lacking peak match fitness and is expected to start from the substitute bench.

articles.title: Tommy Edman Delivers Again When Dodgers Need Him Most vs. Nationals
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Washington Nationals, 6-4, in a tightly contested game thanks to Tommy Edman.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Washington Nationals, 6-4, in a tightly contested game.

The Dodgers put up two runs in the first inning, coming on two different RBI singles, one from Teoscar Hernandez and Hunter Feduccia.

From then on, the offense would really struggle until the seventh inning, when Tommy Edman hit the go-ahead home run to give LA a 5-4 lead.

Edman has been hitting leadoff over the last three games without Shohei Ohtani, and he has overall impressed with timely hitting.

Mookie Betts had another multi-hit game, and his newfound swing is delivering a big boost for a lacking offense on the whole.

Once again, the offense didn't create many chances, but when they had opportunities, they delivered. The Dodgers went 3-for-8 with runners in scoring position.

For a team missing Max Muncy and Dalton Rushing due to late scratches, it was a good performance, all things considered.

Pitching-wise, it was rough for Tyler Glasnow, who pitched six innings and allowed four runs. He had eight strikeouts, but six hits and three walks as well.

He threw only 56 strikes out of his 96 pitches, struggling with command badly early on, but he settled in well.

Glasnow finished with just 12 whiffs on 36 swings, though 20 called strikes helped him out tremendously. Only 42% of pitches were in the zone on the night, and with little chase, just 23%; it was tough to get in favorable counts.

In the end, it was a good step forward for someone making his third start after months without pitching.

After him, Alex Vessia took the bat, striking out two hitters and allowing one hit, while Evan Phillips put up a clean inning, and Tanner Scott got the save despite allowing a run in the ninth inning and almost blowing it.

Scott got two strikeouts to start, but then he allowed a single, another single that scored a run, and then a double to put runners on second and third.

After five pitches, he got the strikeout and secured a third straight win for LA.

The Dodgers will aim to secure the series sweep on Sunday.

articles.title: College football media flabbergasted by Michigan’s controversial Hail Mary win over WMU
articles.summary: “It’s the attack from the MAC! Western Michigan sends shockwaves across the college football world!” That was NBC’s Noah Eagle as the WMU Broncos finished of...
articles.body:
"It's the attack from the MAC! Western Michigan sends shockwaves across the college football world!"

That was NBC's Noah Eagle as the WMU Broncos finished off their epic upset win over the mighty Michigan Wolverines in the Big House on Saturday night.

Michigan tried in vain to win on a Hail Mary attempt to the end zone, but quarterback Bryce Underwood's pass fell to the ground as the clock hit 0:00, cementing the 12-7 outcome.

Immediately after the play, the stadium announcer said it was under review. And a few moments later, the head referee stepped to the middle of the field and said, "After review, there's one second remaining in the game. Third down."

NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay was confused as to what the referees were seeing to add a second back on, but regardless, the two teams returned to the field for what would undoubtedly be one more Hail Mary attempt. And then…

Underwood heaved the ball toward the end zone, JJ Buchanan somehow hauled it in amid a sea of Western Michigan defenders, and the Wolverines had pulled out the shocking victory, 13-12.

Naturally, confusion reigned as no explanation was given for why the second was added back to the clock, especially when both the game clock and NBC's clock (per McAulay) read 0:00 before the ball even reached a player.

All across the college media world, the reactions were as spicy and flabbergasted as you might expect.

You better believe the reactions and conversation around this controversial finish are only just beginning.

articles.title: Luka Doncic's leadership for the Los Angeles Lakers gets a spotlight from Collin Sexton
articles.summary: Luka Doncic has become a superb leader for the Lakers over the summer.
articles.body:
Now that LeBron James has left the Los Angeles Lakers , the team is now clearly centered on Luka Doncic. He is the superstar now, and he seems to be embracing the leadership role, with the four-time Finals MVP moving east to join the Philadelphia 76ers .

So far, so good for Doncic because he has been taking his new role seriously. In fact, he even brought a lot of his Lakers teammates to Slovenia in the summer. It was a big deal for Luka and his teammates because it shows he is willing to lead them in the 2026-27 season.

Collin Sexton reveals that Luka Doncic is taking his leadership role seriously

It was clear in the 2026 Playoffs that the Lakers would have gone further if they had a healthy Doncic. They managed to make it into the second round, but they fell to the Oklahoma City Thunder in a dominant sweep. James and Reaves tried their best, but they lacked the firepower.

While James has left the Lakers, Doncic is back and healthy. He was the #1 guy for the Lakers since they traded for him in February 2025. Now that LeBron is not on the Lakers, it is time for Luka to step up and be the star while also assuming the leadership role.

As a new teammate, Collin Sexton was excited to be part of the Lakers roster alongside Doncic. In just the first few weeks of him being a Laker, he is already meshing well with his teammates, especially during the team-building activities they did in Slovenia, Doncic's home country.

"For Luka to do that, that just shows a true leader. And you can tell that's the role that he wants to fall into this season and be the one to lead us. It was amazing. It was definitely cool. It definitely was one of those experiences that I would love to go back. I think it was something that you never expect," Sexton said to ESPN Los Angeles regarding Doncic's leadership so far .

This is a good sign for the Lakers because they want to be competitive in the 2026-27 season. No one is giving them a shot compared to the Thunder and the San Antonio Spurs . However, having Doncic as the star player and willing leader is an advantage that can go a long way.

articles.title: Ben Simmons Open to Staying With Kings Long-Term
articles.summary: Ben Simmons signed a one-year contract with the Sacramento Kings, but he is open to staying with the team long-term if everything goes well.Simmons sat out t...
articles.body:
Ben Simmons signed a one-year contract with the Sacramento Kings, but he is open to staying with the team long-term if everything goes well.

Simmons sat out the 2025-26 season with injuries, but now that he is healthy again, he signed a one-year, $3.5 million veteran's minimum deal with the Kings to return to the NBA.

While many fans and analysts have laughed at the Kings for giving Simmons another chance, given how disappointing his NBA career has been overall, it's still a buy-low opportunity for Sacramento to bring in a former No. 1 overall pick and see if he has anything left in the tank.

If it turns out to be a good fit, then Simmons could stay in California's capital city for longer than one year.

Speaking to Sactown Sports 1140 , ESPN NBA reporter Marc J. Spears explained why Simmons could stay in Sacramento for more than just one season, noting that the Aussie is "a pretty loyal guy," adding that "I think he'd want to stay" if it turned out to be a nice fit between the player and team.

"I think Sacramento offers an opportunity to not only play but to be supported. You go to Sacramento, it's about basketball. You go to Sacramento, I put their fans up with anybody in the world, in terms of the NBA. They eat, sleep, drink (basketball)," Spears said.

How Will Ben Simmons Fare in Sacramento?

Given that Simmons only got a veteran's minimum contract, the financial burden isn't heavy if he doesn't pan out for the team.

But if he does play well, then this could be a steal of a contract for Sacramento, as Simmons is an excellent defensive player who can also chip in some scoring, passing, and rebounding, as he is a well-rounded player.

We all know that shooting the ball has never been Simmons' strength, but if he can provide a solid defensive effort for the Kings and also provide some leadership on and off the court, this could turn out to be a good pairing between the team and the player.

articles.title: JJ Buchanan explains Michigan's game-winning Hail Mary catch
articles.summary: Michigan wide receiver Buchanan reflects on his game winning Hail Mary catch that saved the Wolverines on Saturday.
articles.body:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. -- All during fall camp, the buzz was that Utah transfer wide receiver could catch anything thrown his way. All contested catches appeared to be his domain, but considering that was something that happened behind closed doors, it couldn't be believed until it was seen.

And on Saturday night, he made it apparent that it wasn't just bluster.

The sophomore from Utah had six catches for 126 yards, but the most important was the game-winner -- a walk-off Hail Mary that he could with zeroes on the clock from 47 yards out. Often, when players make big, career-making plays, the thought is they have a lot running through their mind: evade this defender, get the ball in your hands, come down with it -- et cetera. However, for Buchanan, no such thing happened.

He thought he just had to run down into the end zone and do what he had to do. That was that.

"I just got to run down, and hopefully the ball finds you and the ball found me," Buchanan said. "I don't know what I saw. I just saw the ball, and I attacked it."

Michigan football vs. Western Michigan: Best photos from 13-12 win

Well, just that he had to be the one to finish the play with a touchdown. That's that.

"Just I got like the ball's got to end up in one of our hands," Buchanan said. "That's really the only thing that could have been going through my mind. So, when the ball was in the air, I had to find someone, and it found me"

While that's rather simplistic, obviously Buchanan knew the stakes. This is something that he's worked on -- ensuring that when it comes between him and a defender -- or several -- he's got to be the one to finish on the positive end.

He was pleased to be the one to give the Wolverines the victory, but he's also none too pleased that it came down to that.

"Man, like the team needed a play," Buchanan said. "And, like I said before, there's not too much practice that goes into that. You kind of just run to a spot and look for the ball. And so when I caught it, just relief. Like everyone's been saying, like it shouldn't have been that close. And I feel like our priorities are maybe somewhere else. But it was surreal. Like it was a surreal moment."

He'll need to continue his ascent if Michigan football is going to have a chance in Week 2, as Oklahoma is set to come to The Big House for a big Big Ten-SEC showdown.

articles.title: USF’s defense lifts Bulls to win over FIU in Brian Hartline’s debut
articles.summary: USF’s defense dictated the game and aided the offense as the Bulls bested Florida International, 19-9, in Brian Hartline’s head coaching debut Saturday at Ra...
articles.body:
USF's defense dictated the game and aided the offense as the Bulls bested Florida International, 19-9, in Brian Hartline's head coaching debut Saturday at Raymond James Stadium.

The difference a year — or more accurately, a massive roster and staff overhaul — can make was clear.

In 2025, the Bulls boasted a high-octane offensive operation. Their lowest scoring effort at Raymond James last season was a 34-point performance in their season-opening win over Boise State, and they entered Saturday having won seven consecutive home games by at least 25 points.

On Saturday, they won by 10 and their longest play went for 14 yards.

The offensive performance was lackluster, but the defense, now led by Josh Aldridge, delivered three turnovers and four fourth-down stops to lift USF to a comfortable victory.

"I've been a part of a lot of boring Week 1s, to say the least," Hartline said postgame. "Find a way to win, and grow from there."

He admitted he'd like to see the offense be more productive, but added he will never bemoan a win.

"The standards are where they need to be," Hartline said. "I think we'll continue to grow and work and look forward to the growth we're gonna have from Week 1 to Week 2, and then it better grow again from Week 2 to Week 3. And we'll continue that process through the whole season."

Some of the drastic differences in offense seemed intentional. Where Alex Golesh, now the head coach at Auburn, might have seen the opportunity to convert a short fourth down or even attempt a tricky fake punt, Hartline and offensive coordinator Tim Beck saw an opportunity to call on Nico Gramatica, their trusty kicker, or pin the Panthers deep in their own territory.

There was however, a level of offensive execution USF did not deliver Saturday night that can't be attributed to a difference in approach. The Bulls ran 56 offensive plays but generated only 208 yards.

"We got to make sure we can sustain and have longer drives," Hartline said. "Every time you're kicking a field goal, you're that much closer to letting somebody back in the game."

The Bulls' run-heavy attack largely was stifled all evening. D.J. Crowther, a transfer from Dartmouth, and Jason Collins Jr., a transfer from Morgan State, saw a nearly even split of the workload, with 14 and 17 carries, respectively. Collins went for 59 yards, averaging 3.5 yards a carry, and Crowther went for 42, averaging 3 per attempt, and scored a touchdown.

Quarterback Michael Van Buren Jr. finished 11 of 18 for 100 yards and seven carries for 7 yards in his USF debut.

"There's probably some opportunities he would probably want to have back, but ... he took care of the football," Hartline said. "And that was the No. 1 job description for Mike."

Hartline said he wanted to be mindful of how much he exposed Van Buren to in his USF debut, similarly to how he approached Julian Sayin's debut at Ohio State last season.

"Really proud of the way he operated the offense," Hartline said of Van Buren. "We'll grow from there."

Tayvion Beasley's third-quarter interception was the game's most pivotal moment. USF led only by three, and the offense sputtered on its first two second-half positions. FIU had put together a lengthy 14-play drive to start the half, and while it ultimately ended with a field goal, the Panthers' offense threatened to score again.

But a screen play set up on the right sideline was botched, as Beasley anticipated JJ Kohl's quick throw and the quarterback failed to abandon the script.

That set up USF at FIU's 35-yard line. The offense was far from prolific, but a methodical nine-play scoring drive ended in a 1-yard touchdown run from Crowther.

Now working with a 10-point lead, the Bulls defense again delivered in front of an announced crowd of 41,847. Deep in its own territory, FIU attempted to convert a fourth and 1, but Kohl fumbled the quarterback keeper, and the Bulls used that opportunity to tack on another Gramatica field goal and extend their lead.

Van Buren said he was pleased to see the team play "complementary football."

"They just put us in a really good position," Van Buren said of the defense. "When they make a play, we got to have their backs and go make a play as well."

The first half belonged to Gramatica, a familiar name on a roster with dozens of transfers. The junior made two first-half field goals to put USF ahead 6-0 after 30 minutes of play, both opportunities that came after fourth-down stands from the defense.

Gramatica's first conversion — a 37-yard attempt — was the final play of the first quarter and came after a failed FIU fourth and 5. Wideout Greg Gaines III, a Tampa Bay Tech graduate, found room in the middle of the field, but couldn't connect with Kohl.

Gramatica's second kick, this time from 53 yards, came after cornerback Amarion Fortenberry, a transfer from Kansas State, foiled another FIU fourth-down attempt with a tackle for loss. It was Gramatica's second-longest field goal of his career and his sixth from beyond 50 yards.

"Really proud of the guys," Hartline said. "Winning's never easy. Never take it for granted because if you do, it's fleeting."

articles.title: Tommy Edman and Teoscar Hernández lead Dodgers past Nationals 6-5 in Shohei Ohtani's absence
articles.summary: Tommy Edman and Teoscar Hernández provided key hits in Shohei Ohtani's absence as the Los Angeles Dodgers rallied for a 6-5 victory over the Washington Natio...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Tommy Edman and Teoscar Hernández provided key hits in Shohei Ohtani's absence as the Los Angeles Dodgers rallied for a 6-5 victory over the Washington Nationals on Saturday night.

Edman put the Dodgers ahead with a three-run homer in the seventh inning out of Ohtani's regular leadoff spot, and Hernández had an RBI single in the first while replacing the two-way superstar at designated hitter.

Ohtani remains uncertain to play in Sunday's series finale, with a move to the injured list possible.

Dylan Crews and Daylen Lile each had an RBI double for the Nationals, and Cade Cavalli pitched six strong innings following a rocky start. Cavalli retired 15 of the last 16 batters he faced.

Keibert Ruiz had a run-scoring single against his former team but Washington lost its third consecutive game.
